name: T11c — Touch haptics
description:
Depends on: T11b.

Touch-control haptics only (native Android View path):
- Add `runtime/input/touch_haptics.*`: a host-testable policy with an injected sink. A new face-button, L/R, START/SELECT or d-pad touch-down requests exactly one short tick; analog-stick down/movement, edit drag/resize, release and slide-between-controls request none.
- `TouchOverlayView` executes the tick with `performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK)` (API 26+, respects the system touch-feedback setting), guarded by `isHapticFeedbackEnabled()`. No vibrator or disabled setting is a silent no-op.
- No time-based throttle: each distinct touch-down must survive, otherwise a rapid press is swallowed. The platform haptic API coalesces at the hardware layer; a failed/absent vibration must never throw, block input, or leave a pressed state stuck.
- Host policy tests with an injected sink: one request per button/dpad down; none for stick, edit, move, slide or release; disabled/absent sink is a no-op; five rapid downs produce five requests; a throwing sink is caught and later presses still work.
- Physical phone QA: observe a short tick on every button/dpad press; disable system touch feedback and confirm silence while input still works. The x86_64 emulator proves only the no-op path.
- Explicitly exclude gamepad rumble, `sceRumble`, and battle haptics; those are deferred to T13/M5.

Reference set: Yakumo's MIT `touch_action::take_haptics` and `platform/android_jni.cpp` `haptic_tick` are the behavioral pattern; Android `HapticFeedbackConstants`/`performHapticFeedback` and the system touch-feedback setting are the platform contract. PPSSPP/Dolphin vibration behavior is behavioral only (GPL; no code copied). Adjust Yakumo's swipe/D-pad-direction feedback to the chosen new-touch-down-only scope.

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): tests observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "performHapticFeedback" --extension java`; `gh search code "HapticFeedbackConstants" --extension java`; `gh search code "isHapticFeedbackEnabled" --extension java`; `gh search code "VibrationEffect.createOneShot" --extension java`; `gh search issues "Android touch haptics"`.

Device validation: see `android/AGENTS.md` — emulator is for initial bring-up; physical arm64 phone QA is required at sprint end and recorded in `docs/qa/`. Reproducible emulator: `scripts/android/emulator.sh`.
result:
T11c complete (implementation df27849, QA 91578b5).

- runtime/input/touch_haptics.*: host-testable policy with an injected sink. A new face-button, L/R, START/SELECT or d-pad down calls the sink exactly once; the stick, slide/move, edit gestures and release never do. No time-based throttle, so a genuine rapid press is not swallowed; a missing, disabled or throwing sink is a no-op and cannot change input state.
- TouchOverlay::touch_down now returns the hit control; the JNI bridge returns the policy result. The Android View uses performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackConstants.CLOCK_TICK) after checking Settings.System.HAPTIC_FEEDBACK_ENABLED; a disabled setting or missing vibrator is silent while input still works. Debug logs name performed/disabled.
- Red-first: tests/input/touch_haptics_tests.cpp and tests/test_touch_haptics.py were added before touch_haptics.* existed; configure failed on the missing source, then the policy went green. Contracts cover the control table, one tick per down, five rapid downs, disabled/absent/throwing sinks and TouchOverlay hit results.
- Device QA on M2102K1AC (arm64, API 34), app df27849: JNI/Java logged touch_haptic performed=true; dumpsys vibrator_manager recorded com.gungnir.recomp, usage TOUCH, performHapticFeedback/View#performHapticFeedback, TEXTURE_TICK, 24ms. L/R/START/SELECT plus four d-pad directions counted 8/8; five rapid Cross taps counted 5/5. Stick drag and edit drag/resize counted 0. With haptic_feedback_enabled=0 the View logged touch_haptic_disabled and no effect appeared; re-enabling restored the tick. Manual physical feel passed. Report docs/qa/2026-10-31-t11c-touch-haptics.md.
- Gates: full suite 136/136 OK; Android clean-checkout APK gate passes; repository_check PASS (323 files). The x86_64 emulator exposes a virtual vibrator so it exercised the tick path; no-vibrator no-op is covered by the absent-sink host contract and performHapticFeedback returning false.

References: TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, pinned b61852a) touch_action haptics and android_jni haptic_tick as behavioral patterns (no code copied); Android HapticFeedbackConstants/performHapticFeedback and Settings.System.HAPTIC_FEEDBACK_ENABLED contract; PPSSPP/Dolphin vibration behavior behavioral only (GPL, no code or assets copied). Gaps: gamepad rumble, sceRumble and battle haptics are deferred to T13/M5; consolidated T11 gate is T11e.

name: T6i — Async file I/O completion (sceIoLseekAsync and friends)
description:
The T6h boot advances to 25,546 dispatches / 17 flips and stops at Missing HLE import IoFileMgrForUser::sceIoLseekAsync (NID_0x71B19E77). Implement the async IoFileMgr surface title-scoped: lseek/read/write/open/close async variants with deterministic deferred completion through the kernel (no sleeps masking races), correct SceIoStat/lseek semantics, and cancellation/error paths. Add red-first contracts in tests/hle, extend the bounded boot, and record the next blocker in docs/BRINGUP.md. Evidence: docs/BRINGUP.md 2026-10-30 T6h entry.

ABI cross-check (2026-10-30): zPSP-Dev/Zig-PSP's generated
`src/c/module/IoFileMgrForUser.zig` (MIT) documents the result-pointer
conventions for `sceIoPollAsync`, `sceIoWaitAsync`, `sceIoWaitAsyncCB` and
`sceIoGetAsyncStat`; useful when pinning T6i's asynchronous completion
contract against a second PSPSDK-derived source. It is an ABI reference only,
not an implementation to copy.

Reference leads (2026-10-30, found with `gh search issues`):
- PPSSPP #12549/#12506/#136/#153 describe the async IoFileMgr lifecycle and
  its regressions. Behavioral oracle in `Core/HLE/sceIo.cpp`: `sceIoOpenAsync`
  returns the fd directly; async read/write/lseek set a per-fd result and are
  not complete until Wait/Poll/GetAsyncStat; `sceIoWaitAsync`/`CB` write a
  64-bit result and return 0; `sceIoPollAsync` returns 1 while pending and 0
  when complete; `sceIoGetAsyncStat(fd,poll,res)` waits when poll=0 and
  reports 1 when pending; `sceIoCloseAsync` defers fd release until the
  completion wait. `sceIoLseekAsync` takes an s64 offset; bad whence returns
  INVAL; a second async op while busy returns ASYNC_BUSY. Treat as HYPOTHESIS
  until pinned by our own red-first contracts.
- wizardengineer/psprecomp #63 documents a static-recompiler async-I/O and
  scheduler race (busy-poll vs wait) to avoid when choosing the deferred
  completion policy.
- cspspemu #70 is only a stub-first discussion; do not copy that approach.
- snuri00/psp-web-recomp (MIT), `profile/host/io.cpp`, is a static-recompiler
  HLE with the same contract: async calls return immediately; WaitAsync writes
  a 64-bit result; PollAsync returns 1 while pending and completes through the
  same path; CloseAsync marks the fd closing and erases it after the wait;
  plain reads complete inline. Useful as a second implementation to diff
  against, but it completes inline rather than deferring.
- psce4all (GPL-2.0) and psprism (GPL-3.0) confirm the NID/signature table
  (`CB05F8D6` GetAsyncStat, `E23EEC33` WaitAsync, `3251EA56` PollAsync,
  `35DBD746` WaitAsyncCB, `89AA9906` OpenAsync, `FF5940B6` CloseAsync,
  `71B19E77` LseekAsync, `A0B5A7C2` ReadAsync, `0FACAB19` WriteAsync) but
  their handlers are stubs; use only as an ABI cross-check.
- jpd002/Play- (PSF player) has sync I/O only, not useful here.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.
result:
T6i complete (commit a538016).

- Implemented async IoFileMgr: open/read/write/lseek/close plus lseek32, with Wait/CB/Poll/GetAsyncStat collection. Host I/O completes synchronously, but the result is staged per descriptor and the descriptor stays busy until collected; close defers release to collection; failed async opens return a descriptor and deliver the error through Wait. Kernel error codes for busy/no-async/closed/bad-whence.
- Added reset of the IO descriptor table per registration and extracted shared read/write/seek helpers so sync and async paths cannot drift.
- Red-first async contracts in tests/hle/kernel_tests.cpp: open/read/lseek/close staging, poll, getAsyncStat, waitCB, busy, failed open, no-async, closed descriptor, invalid whence.
- Boot: 25,546 -> 26,058 dispatches, 21 vblanks, 19 flips; 154/215 imports bound, 82 executed, zero missing/silent NIDs. Executed async calls: sceIoLseekAsync, sceIoReadAsync, sceIoPollAsync. sceIoOpenAsync and WaitAsync are bound/tested but not executed by this title yet.
- Remaining IoFileMgr gaps counted: sceIoDread and sceIoIoctl.
- Next blocker: sceUtility::sceUtilitySavedataInitStart (NID_0x50C4CD57), tracked as T6k.
- Full suite 64/64 green; repository_check PASS (175 files).

name: T8c — Texture dump mode with hash-keyed PNG export
description:
Depends on: T8a.

Add dump mode to the runtime texture path: every decoded texture is written
to user storage as a PNG plus a textures.ini manifest (PPSSPP semantics as a
behavioral reference: stable content key, dimensions, format). The key must
cover geometry, pixel format, swizzle/bufw, texel bytes and all CLUT bytes so
a palette change produces a new key. Dumps go under a configured user
directory; nothing game-derived is committed.

PNG I/O must use an existing codec, never a hand-written one (AGENTS.md hard
limit 0): prefer system libpng with a version check, or a pinned MIT/public-
domain library recorded through the dependency/provenance process. Record the
choice in the T8 result and docs.

Tests (red first, synthetic TPL fixture):
- TC-8.2 dump half: dump to a temp dir, re-decode the PNG, pixels match the
  in-memory decode exactly.
- Two runs produce identical keys and bytes; changing one CLUT entry changes
  the key; a repeat dump does not overwrite a user replacement (T8d).

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "textures.ini" --extension cpp`; `gh search
code "texture dumping" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "texture
replacement hash"`; `gh search code "texture_collection" --extension cpp`.

Refs: psprecore `texture_collection.cpp`/`texture_replacement.cpp` (MIT,
behavioral reference only), PPSSPP texture replacement docs (semantics), T7
texture cache key tests. Gotchas: §7A.2 (no game content), §7B.3, §7F.3.
result:
Added runtime/tex/{png.hpp,png.cpp,dump.hpp,dump.cpp} and the gungnir_tex_png/gungnir_tex_dump targets, built when system libpng is available (1.6.59 on the host; zlib/libpng license, not vendored). read_png normalises RGB/RGBA/gray/palette/16-bit PNGs to RGBA8; write_png emits deterministic RGBA8 PNGs.

Dump mode hashes a content key (FNV-1a v1 over pixel format, swizzle, width, height, buffer width, CLUT format/mask, palette count/format, texel bytes and CLUT bytes) excluding live GE sampler state, so replacement lookups remain stable when clamp/filter changes. It writes new/<KEY>.png and appends textures.ini entries ([options] version=1 hash=gungnir64, [hashes] KEY = new/KEY.png) without duplicating keys (case-normalised). Existing PNGs are compared pixel-for-pixel: identical files are skipped, different files fail key_collision, corrupt files fail existing_png_invalid, so dump never overwrites user data. Batch dumps handle multiple textures; duplicate same-content keys are collapsed, different content under one key fails key_collision.

Tests in tests/tex/dump_tests.cpp: key stability and sensitivity to CLUT/texel/buffer-width/swizzle/format, live-sampler independence, PNG round-trip, manifest creation/de-duplication, batch dumps, CLUT-change dumps, collision/corrupt rejection and named invalid inputs. Mutation: removing palette bytes from the key fails 'CLUT bytes change the key'. Local dump check on six user containers wrote 14 textures and re-read every PNG. Full suite 77/77 green; repository_check PASS (223 files).

References used: PPSSPP PR #8715, the texture-replacement wiki and GPU/Common/TextureReplacer.cpp for [options]/[hashes]/[hashranges]/mipmap/empty-filename semantics (behavior only; no code adopted), psprecore runtime/src/gpu/texture_collection.cpp (MIT) for the content-hash + PNG + index dump shape, LiinkPK/Texture-Replacement-Tool-for-PPSSPP for replacement-pack workflow (binary-only, no source adopted), and libpng for the codec. Docs: docs/TEXTURE_REPLACEMENT.md records the layout and the explicit non-compatibility with PPSSPP's 24-hex key.

name: T14a — Manual QA campaign: QA.md, device matrix, red-first fixes, suspend/resume + 30-min soak
description:
Part of T14 (plan §5 and §8.3). Owns TC-14.1 (from-scratch run), TC-14.2 (matrix and cold boots) and TC-14.3 (suspend/resume and soak). Physical-device QA is mandatory; the emulator never closes this task.

# T14a — Manual QA campaign

**Depends on:** T13b, T13c, T13d, T13e.

**Goal.** Every matrix cell has a dated, signed report; the documented from-scratch pipeline reaches the title screen and menu on the adb device; every finding is fixed red-first or tracked.

**Work.**
- Write `docs/QA.md`: the standard script plus the Gungnir-specific script (title → menu → first gameplay transition). Cover cold boot, touch menu, gamepad menu (paired + built-in handheld), overlay hide-on-pad, suspend/resume rendering recovery, rotation ignored, save/load, touch haptic tick, rumble status (from T13g), audio smoke, 30-minute soak, and thermal/battery observations. Include the evidence/sign-off template and the three-cold-boot rule.
- Run the matrix: x86_64 emulator (SwiftShader) plus at least one physical Adreno arm64 phone and one non-Adreno/handheld where available. Ask the user for device access and interaction; use adb and `scripts/android/*`, never xdotool.
- TC-14.1: execute the documented from-scratch pipeline from `docs/BUILDING.md` on this machine, install the APK, and reach the title screen plus menu input on the adb device.
- File one dated `docs/qa/<date>-<device>.md` per session with model, Android version, GPU/driver (system or user zip + version), build SHA, tester, steps, expected/actual, pass/fail counts, screenshot SHA-256 (images stay in gitignored `build/qa/`). No game frames in the repo.
- Run three consecutive cold boots per device. Run suspend/resume cycles and a 30-minute soak on at least one physical device; record crash/thermal/audio counters and a recording hash, not frames.
- Fix findings red-first wherever host-testable (reproducing test before the fix); file device-only defects as tracked dex tasks and link them from the report. Every finding ends with a regression test or an open defect ID.
- Include the Android memstick save/load path and the audio smoke in at least one cell; record named gaps rather than passing them silently.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- A QA-report structure test (`tests/test_qa_reports.py`) validates required fields, matrix cells, date/build SHA, and pass/fail counts; it fails before the first report exists.
- Any host-testable finding gets a red reproduction in the owning suite before its fix.
- Re-run the three cold boots after every fix; a regression re-opens the cell.

**Acceptance / evidence.** TC-13.1, TC-14.2 and TC-14.3 pass with dated reports; every matrix cell is signed; no game frames or hashes of game content are committed; every finding has a red test or a tracked open defect.

**Guardrails.** "CI is green" is not device evidence; one successful boot is not evidence. Do not fabricate a device result — record what was actually run. No xdotool; ask the user for GUI interaction when needed. PPSSPP is an oracle only.

**Docs.** `docs/QA.md`, `docs/qa/<date>-<device>.md`, `docs/BRINGUP.md`, `docs/PROGRESS.md` notes.

**Reference projects (QA and oracle tooling).**
- `Jstar269/hst-decomp` (GPL-3.0) — milestone/evidence discipline and the ratchet format.
- `zxyandreay/azazel6` (MIT) — VERIFIED/HYPOTHESIS evidence labels and bounded-run reporting.
- `BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp` (GPL-2.0-or-later) — `ppsspp_ws.py`, `drive.py`, `pace_test.py` for oracle input/pacing, run out-of-tree.
- `AdamFull/ff7ccrecomp` (MIT) — `scripts/regress.ps1` and recording/replay regression shape.
- `Tzeentchnet/MetalGearAcid2-Recomp` (GPL-2.0-or-later, Windows-only) — fixed-profile `.pad` input scripts and benchmark/QA shape; behavioral only.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Read the matching source with `gh repo read-file` / `gh repo read-dir`, never raw.githubusercontent.com. Record the references used in the task result; if a reference shapes the design, add a prose note to `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).
Specific first searches: `gh search code "docs/QA.md"`, `gh search code "cold boots" --filename "*.md"`, `gh search issues "dumpsys thermalservice"`, `gh search issues "adb shell dumpsys battery"`, `gh search code "SCREENSHOT_SHA256"`. Review `Jstar269/hst-decomp` and `azazel6` for evidence-label and QA-report shape; keep the matrix Gungnir-specific. For the soak, `gh search issues "Adreno 30 minute thermal throttle"` is a useful behavioral reference.

name: T10f — Driver docs, named gaps and T10 closure gate
description:
Depends on: T10a–T10e.

Finish `docs/ANDROID_DRIVERS.md`: what driver zips are, where users get them, risks (third-party binaries, thermal/stability, no warranty), supported schemas, import/selection UI, private-storage rule, fallback and named-error troubleshooting, and the no-bundling policy. Add `tests/test_adreno_suite.py` consolidating TC-10.1–TC-10.4 (host tests + doc contract + repository guard) and mutation evidence (system bypass mutated to call custom; ABI check removed; fallback uses the failed handle). name: Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan
description:
(Complete plan lives at .dex/plan.md in this repo; §3 reference-projects table is omitted below only for size — see the file. Subtasks T1–T13 each carry their plan section.)

# Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan

**Target:** Gungnir (USA) — *Gungnir: Inferno of the Demon Lance and the War of Heroes*, ULUS-10592
**Goal:** Static recompilation of the game's Allegrex code to native C++, running on Android — from the user's own `game.chd` to a boot on an adb-connected device.
**First milestone (locked):** title screen rendered on device + menu input navigable (touch + gamepad).
**Plan date:** 2026-10-30. Source: 14-project discovery survey (see §3).

---

## 0. Hard constraints (non-negotiable)

1. **No proprietary content, code, or work is ever committed.** No game ISO/CHD/ELF/PRX, no decrypted modules, no game assets (DAR contents, TPL textures, VAG audio, script `.bin`), no game text (original or translated), no game screenshots, no Sony firmware, no PGF fonts, no KIRK/DRM keys, no Adreno driver binaries, no generated recompilation output (which is a derivative of the copyrighted executable).
2. The repo contains only: original tooling and runtime we author, third-party code with licenses preserved and attributed, synthetic fixtures of our own authorship, documentation, and scripts that operate on **user-supplied local files**.
3. Decryption of `~PSP` modules runs **out-of-process** using user-supplied tools (pspdecrypt / PPSSPP devtools). We ship no decryption implementation and no keys. Same for Adreno driver `.zip`s: user-supplied, extracted to app-private storage, never bundled or committed.
4. Enforcement is structural, not aspirational: `.gitignore` with rationale, `tools/repository_check.py` (extension + magic-byte + blob-size + ignore-rule audit) in CI, secret scanning, and fail-closed CI (`exit 77` skips) for tests that need private game input.
5. Game-derived facts that are acceptable to publish: disc identity (size 262,766,592 B, CRC32 `183F3EDC`, redump-recorded), format field layouts, NID values, guest addresses and record sizes (RE facts). Binaries, hashes of binaries pinned as "the expected dump", and content derived from them stay local.
6. **No clean-room reimplementations.** If work reduces to implementing a format, codec, or protocol that existing tools or libraries already implement, **stop and ask before writing anything**: use the existing tool out-of-process, or adopt an audited open-source implementation with provenance. Clean-room reimplementation is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md hard limit #0).

## 1. Decisions locked (2026-10-30)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Foundation | Adopt an **MIT-licensed PSPRecomp-framework core** (jessicanataliagta/PSPRecomp lineage; TeamGDB/Yakumo framework subset is the same lineage, more mature). We write: Gungnir profile, Android shell, Vulkan renderer, driver loader, texture/shader systems. |
| Project license | **GPL-3.0-or-later** (max reuse freedom: MIT + BSD + LGPL-dynamic + GPL-2.0-or-later + GPL-3.0 sources; rejects CC BY-NC-SA and unattributed code) |
| Android baseline | **minSdk 26, Vulkan 1.1 required**, AAudio available; ABIs `arm64-v8a` + `x86_64` (emulator) |
| Renderer | **Vulkan-only** (no GL ES fallback); software rasterizer kept as parity oracle; post-processing chain (upscale + LCD/scanline shaders) after GE compositing |
| Audio | AAudio (Android) / SDL audio (desktop); ATRAC3(+) via LGPL `at3_standalone`-class decoder with notices |
| Game data on device | SAF document-tree picker **or** `adb push` to `getExternalFilesDir()`. **No** `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` |
| Adreno drivers | User-supplied `.zip` ICDs (Mesa Turnip / Qualcomm-style) loaded via custom Vulkan loader; per-driver selection; fail-closed fallback to system driver |
| Input | Touch overlay (editable layout) + SDL3 gamepad with per-device profiles (Ayn/Ayaneo-class handhelds) + keyboard/mouse (desktop dev); rumble/haptics via SDL gamepad rumble + Android Vibrator fallback |
| Textures | Hash-keyed dump→replace pipeline (PPSSPP `textures.ini` semantics) + high-res font-atlas re-rasterization for dialog text (Gungnir stores text in TPL atlases and baked into TPL images) |
| Disc input | **Intake accepts ISO only.** `game.chd` is converted once, user-side — e.g. [CHDStudio](https://github.com/purelogiccode/CHDStudio) (GUI, recommended) or `chdman extractcd` (MAME CLI). Our pipeline never parses CHD. Converter correctness is *verified, not trusted* — the identity gate (size + CRC32) validates whatever produced the ISO. |
| Code reuse | **Adopt, don't reimplement.** Clean-room implementations of existing formats/codecs/protocols are **not sanctioned** without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0): use existing tools out-of-process (CHDStudio/chdman) or adopt audited open-source code with provenance (Yakumo MIT subset → `third_party/yakumo/`). Applies to everything upcoming too (e.g. PGF parsing, ATRAC3, image codecs, JSON) — check the reference projects and library landscape first, always. |
| Testing | **Red-first (TDD where relevant):** the failing test lands before the implementation, and is confirmed red for the expected reason. Regression fixes start from a failing reproduction. No task closes with untested behavior. |
| Device validation | **Mandatory manual QA on an adb device** before any milestone touching device behavior can close — structured, recorded QA (build ID, device, steps, expected/actual, sign-off), never "CI is green" alone |

## 2. Target facts — Gungnir (USA)

Facts from the discovery survey (kreycai/gungnir-ptbr format docs, redump, PPSSPP logs). These shape the whole plan:

- **Disc:** UMD ISO 9660, 262,766,592 B, CRC32 `183F3EDC` (redump 29734). The local `game.chd` is an LZMA CHD of this disc (header verified: `MComprHD` v5, `lzma`). JP is ULJM-05779 (v1.01) — different offsets everywhere; this plan targets **USA only**.
- **`PSP_GAME/SYSDIR/EBOOT.BIN`:** 3,336,096 B at ISO offset `0x110000`, `~PSP`-encrypted (magic `0x5053507E`); `BOOT.BIN` sibling is the plaintext form on some discs. Decrypted form: PRX ELF `e_type 0xFFA0`, segment 0 at file offset `0xC0` with `vaddr = file_offset − 0xC0`, relocation section type `0x70000020` (entries 8 B: `r_offset:u32, r_info:u32`, types **2 = R_MIPS_32, 5 = HI16, 6 = LO16**). ~3,552 strings live in the EBOOT (vaddr `0x19F000–0x1D8000` region).
- **USRDIR archives (DAR format):** `ini.dar` (61 files incl. font atlases `font11pt.tpl`/`font12pt.tpl`), `voice.dar` (voice audio), `data.dar` (~44 MB, plaintext, 1,295 `.tpl` textures + ~13,998 strings + script `.bin`s), plus `INSDIR/DATA.DAR`. DAR header = 4×u32 LE `[nfiles, data_start, names_off, table_off]`; entries = 16 B `[name_off, stored_size, decomp_size, data_off]`; zlib per entry when `decomp_size > stored_size`; **`stored_size == 0` means stored uncompressed** (real size in `decomp_size`).
- **Text:** fullwidth Shift-JIS (cp932), NUL-terminated; engine break commands `5C 6E` in DAR data, `0x3B` in EBOOT. Script `.bin` files (`event/`, `map/`, `worldmap/`, `setup*/`) = `[u32 type, u32 n, u32 table_off=12]` + n absolute u32 offsets + bytecode with absolute-address jumps — **files must not change size** or every pointer/jump must be remapped.
- **Fonts/textures:** TPL containers (0x30 B header; per-texture `H,W,BW,bpp,data_off`), 4bpp PSP-swizzled (16×8 blocks), index-as-alpha, and 8bpp+CLUT. Dialog glyph advance = ink width (width table). UI text is also **baked into images** (actname/tutorial/location pages) — text upscaling has two fronts: font atlas re-rasterization + image texture replacement.
- **Engine/runtime expectations (PPSSPP logs):** calls `sceKernelLoadModule` (PRX overlay tiers needed), "render to area containing texture" (feedback path in GE), one audio-decode quirk. PPSSPP rates it Perfect→Playable — our behavioral oracle.
- **DAR size fields in ISO 9660 directory records are both-endian** (LE + BE 4 bytes later) — any repack must patch both (we don't repack the ISO for recomp, but the asset pipeline touches DARs inside `build/`).

## 4. Architecture & repo layout

```
gungnir-recomp/
├── AGENTS.md                    # single policy authority (hard limits, evidence rules)
├── LICENSE                      # GPL-3.0-or-later
├── .recomp.json                 # recomp.fyi card
├── .gitignore                   # game data / keys / generated code, each with rationale
├── dependencies.json            # pinned third-party revisions (azazel6 pattern)
├── CMakeLists.txt               # desktop + Android shared build (nk_add_title_runtime shape)
├── cmake/Deps.cmake             # fetch-or-reuse with lock+digest
├── configs/nids.csv             # NID registry (BSD pspsdk headers / fetch-with-checksum)
├── tools/
│   ├── repository_check.py      # IP gate (azazel6 adaptation) — CI, pre-push
│   ├── package_notices.py       # generated THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt from one JSON
│   ├── intake/                  # chd→iso→extract→decrypt-hook→manifest
│   ├── analyze, codegen         # analysis + AOT (adopted MIT core + our glue)
│   ├── dar.py, tpl.py           # DAR/TPL readers (user's local files only)
│   ├── textures/                # dump/replace + font-atlas repack
│   └── ghidra/ExportPSPFunctions.java   # optional function census
├── runtime/                     # guest memory, dispatch, interpreter, HLE, GE, post
│   ├── hle/  ge/  post/  input/  audio/  savedata/
│   └── platform/adreno/         # custom Vulkan ICD loader
├── profiles/gungnir/
│   ├── config.toml              # facts-vs-choices (wizardengineer split)
│   └── local/                   # GITIGNORED: hashes, address pins, per-dump data
├── android/                     # Gradle (Kotlin DSL) + JNI shell
├── assets/shaders/{ge,post}/    # committed GLSL (ours), SPIR-V embedded at build
├── assets/input_profiles/       # handheld gamepad profiles (ours)
├── tests/fixtures/              # synthetic Allegrex fixtures of OUR authorship
├── data/milestones.json         # hst-decomp ratchet ledger
├── docs/                        # see §6 documentation checkpoints
└── build/                       # GITIGNORED: game tree, generated code, outputs
```

**Pipeline:** `game.chd` → [T3 intake] → `build/game/` (verified ISO, decrypted ELF, manifest) → [T5 analyze+codegen] → `build/generated/` (chunked C++ TUs) → [T6/T7 runtime] → Linux desktop boot → [T9/T10/T11 Android] → adb device → [T13] title screen.

## 5. Tasks

Each task: dependencies, work, deliverables, test cases (TC), docs checkpoint, reference callouts, gotchas (pointer to §7 register).

**Red-first rule for all tasks (§8.1):** each TC is written and observed red *before* the implementation that satisfies it; bug fixes begin with a reproducing red test; no task below closes with a red or disabled TC. Tasks touching runtime semantics also carry a mutation check.

### T1 — Scaffolding + IP guardrails
**Depends on:** — (first task)
**Work:** git init (keep `game.chd` untracked forever); `LICENSE`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore` (case-insensitive blocks for `*.iso *.chd *.cso *.elf *.prx *.pbp *.bin *.pmf *.at3 *.vag`, `keys/`, `generated/`, `game/`, `PSP_GAME/`, `build/`, `profiles/*/local/`, analysis dumps — with rationale comments, nakagawa style); `tools/repository_check.py` (magic-byte sniff of git index for ELF/`~PSP`/CHD/PE, >1 MB blob rejection, ignore-rule regression tests, secret scan); `docs/LEGAL.md` (the IP charter = §0); `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`; `.recomp.json`.
**Test cases:**
- TC-1.1 `repository_check.py` passes on clean tree.
- TC-1.2 Staging a dummy `.iso`/`.elf`/`~PSP` blob fails the check (each magic recognized).
- TC-1.3 Ignore-rule regression: creating `build/game/x.iso` never appears in `git status`.
- TC-1.4 `game.chd` in workdir is never matched by `git ls-files`.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/LEGAL.md` + `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md` + `AGENTS.md` written **before any code lands**.
**Refs:** nakagawa-recomp (`.gitignore`, AGENTS.md), azazel6 (`repository_check.py`), psprism (`LICENSING.md`), Yakumo (`SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`).
**Gotchas:** §7A.

### T2 — Third-party dependency ledger + license machine
**Depends on:** T1
**Work:** `dependencies.json` pinning: MIT PSPRecomp framework core (choose jessicanataliagta/PSPRecomp `include/+src/` or Yakumo framework subset — record exact commit + provenance), CHD reader (libchdr or chd-rs — audit first), SDL3 (pinned commit, nakagawa `deps.cmake` pattern), stb image, tiny-AES-class public-domain crypto (savedata later), NID name data (BSD pspsdk headers or `pspdev/psp-ghidra-scripts` fetch-with-checksum — **never** copy psprism's unattributed `ppsspp_niddb.xml`; PPSSPP-derived tables are usable under our GPL-3.0 **with attribution**); `cmake/Deps.cmake` (fetch-or-reuse, lock+digest, offline-capable); `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/`; `tools/package_notices.py` → `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`.
**Test cases:**
- TC-2.1 Clean checkout + one command materializes all deps at verified commits (digest check fails on wrong revision).
- TC-2.2 `package_notices.py` output covers every vendored file (CI gate: no unlisted file under `third_party/`).
- TC-2.3 License gate rejects a deliberately added CC BY-NC-SA component.
**Findings (2026-10-30):** first pin landed early with T3: `dependencies.json` + `third_party/yakumo/PROVENANCE.md` + in-tree LICENSE (MIT, pin `b61852a`) — the template the remaining entries (SDL3, CHD reader if ever needed, stb, ATRAC decoder) must follow. **License-implication of §1 Code reuse:** clean-room reimplementations are not sanctioned — where no adoptable code exists for something we need, **stop and ask** (that decision belongs to the user, not the agent).
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/PROVENANCE.md` (per-subtree: upstream, commit, license, disposition).
**Refs:** azazel6 (`dependencies.json`), nakagawa (`deps.cmake` + notice generation), wizardengineer (`fetch-niddb.sh` + checksum), psprism (attribution gap as cautionary tale).
**Gotchas:** §7A.5–A.7.

### T3 — Game intake pipeline (`game.iso` → verified local build tree)
**Depends on:** T1
**Work:** `tools/intake/`: (1) **disc input = ISO only** (locked decision §1: `game.chd` is converted user-side via [CHDStudio](https://github.com/purelogiccode/CHDStudio) or `chdman extractcd`; intake refuses `.chd` with a named error pointing at `docs/INTAKE.md`; we never parse CHD — the identity gate *verifies, not trusts*, the converter); (2) identity gate: size 262,766,592 + CRC32 `183F3EDC`, **fail closed** on mismatch; (3) ISO9660 extract of `PSP_GAME/` tree (EBOOT.BIN, USRDIR `*.dar`, INSDIR, PARAM.SFO — verify disc ID ULUS-10592); (4) decrypt hook — **no decryption code in-repo**; invoke user-supplied pspdecrypt/PPSSPP "Dump decrypted EBOOT.BIN" out-of-process, accept `BOOT.BIN` plaintext or user-provided decrypted ELF, validate PRX shape (`e_type 0xFFA0`, `vaddr = file_offset − 0xC0`, reloc section `0x70000020`, types 2/5/6); (5) `build/game/manifest.json`: module list, SHA-256s, segments, reloc counts, NID import inventory. All outputs under `build/` (gitignored).
**Test cases:**
- TC-3.1 End-to-end on local `game.iso` produces manifest.json with expected module set. *(Covered by `tests/test_intake.py` — written and observed red before implementation.)*
- TC-3.2 Wrong-CRC input (bit-flipped ISO) aborts with named error `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`; `.chd` input aborts with named error `CHD_NOT_SUPPORTED` pointing at CHDStudio.

## 7. Gotchas register

### A. IP / legal
1. `game.chd` already sits in the workdir — it must remain untracked **before the first commit**; T1 is not done until this is mechanically enforced.
2. Generated recomp C++ is a derivative of the copyrighted executable (PSPRecomp-family repos commit 108 MB of it — the anti-pattern we invert). Never committed, never in releases, never in screenshots of game output in-repo.
3. "No game data" claims must match the tree exactly (codepdbh claims it while shipping translated code; alexandercorp links ready-made game files on Google Drive). Documentation claims are evidence-checked in review.
4. EBOOT `expected_sha256` pins stay in gitignored `profiles/gungnir/local/`, not public TOML — pinning a dump hash publicly advertises a specific rip.
5. NID name tables: PPSSPP-derived data is GPL-tainted (usable here with attribution — we are GPL-3.0); psprism's committed `ppsspp_niddb.xml` shows what *unattributed* reuse looks like. Prefer BSD pspsdk-header generation.
6. Reject CC BY-NC-SA material entirely (PSPRecomp's CloudWorks clouds are the cautionary tale) — incompatible with GPL-3.0 and with any commercial future.
7. Third-party **binaries** are never committed (sal063's `SDL3.dll`); build from pinned source; LGPL pieces (FFmpeg/ATRAC) need notices + relink path.

### B. Gungnir formats
1. DAR `stored_size == 0` means **stored uncompressed** (not empty) — the ptbr project zeroed 272 SFX missing this. Never trust `stored_size` alone.
2. DAR in-place rewrite rules: untouched entries keep their `data_off` (internal absolute references); recompressed blobs must fit the original slot (vary zlib params to squeeze); safest = true in-place + zero-fill tail.
3. Script `.bin` files contain absolute-address jumps and pointer tables; **never change file size** without remapping; floats impersonate pointers — only remap 4-aligned pointer-table runs, not "scanned pointers".
4. ISO 9660 directory records carry sizes both-endian (LE field + BE field +4) — patch both or the mount breaks (relevant if we ever repack).
5. Text slots in the EBOOT have real alignment padding; overruns land in relocated pointer words → "Bad Execution Address". The round-trip proof (original text through our writer = byte-identical image) is the writer's acceptance test.
6. Absolute-offset tooling is revision-fragile: every tool runs the identity gate (size + CRC32 `183F3EDC`) first; JP/EU offsets differ entirely.

### C. Static recompiler bug classes (the snuri00 10 + survey additions)
1. Import stub loops: `jal` to a stub must terminate codegen (`break`, not `continue`) — unbounded generation was a real bug class.
2. Data decoded as code: tolerate out-of-range VFPU register indices (read→0, write dropped) instead of build-failing on stripped binaries.
3. Full ISA coverage: one missing opcode (e.g. `ADDI`) is a hard runtime stop — audit every Allegrex encoding up front.
4. Scratchpad at `0x00010000` must be mapped from day one (16 KiB window) or games fault "outside RAM".
5. Function discovery: prologue-after-return heuristics AND HI16/LO16 pair seeding are both required (Gungnir's relocs use types 5/6); mine R_MIPS_32 for stored pointers; seed init/fini arrays; code can live **outside `.text`** (ctors in `.data`).
6. PRX tiers: `sceKernelLoadModule` loads code AOT never saw — per-module translation units + `unregister_functions(start,end)` + safe address reuse (Yakumo's overlay swap is the mature design).
7. VFPU exactness: `vrnd*` PRNG sequence, `vi2us/vi2s/vi2uc/vi2c`, `vt4444/vt5551/vt5650`, prefix quirks (decode-rotation + matrix prefixes bit wizardengineer twice); pin semantics with differential fuzz.
8. Backward local branches compiled as plain `goto` freeze the scheduler — counter-based forced dispatcher exit (~2048 transfers) keeps interrupts/heartbeat alive.
9. Dynamic code is a permanent runtime tier: interpreter + content-hashed block cache with memcmp self-modifying-code checks — not scaffolding to be removed later.
10. Delay-slot shapes differ subtly across engines (hoist+duplicate vs pending-target vs BIDS) — pick one model, test the foreign-owned-slot and branched-into-slot cases explicitly.
11. Jump tables: `jr $reg` ≠ return; recover via DATA xrefs where possible, fall back to runtime dispatch — never guess a table silently.

### D. Runtime / GE
1. Unknown NIDs that silently return 0 mask gaps until they explode in-game (azazel6 bans this) — loud named traps only.
2. Texture `bufw` handling (wizardengineer bug class) and CLUT-inclusive cache keys (sal063) are correctness-critical for Gungnir's 4bpp swizzled atlases.
3. Gungnir's PPSSPP log shows "render to area containing texture" — feedback-path invalidation is a named regression (TC-7.4), not a surprise.
4. Cooperative scheduling first (all surveyed repos converged); preemption is a designed-later phase — but never ship hidden stalls (yield counters + watchdogs).
5. 59.94 Hz pacing: frame = 16,683 µs; a wrong pace desyncs audio and TAS-like determinism tests.

### E. Android platform
1. NDK Clang chokes on huge generated TUs — chunk generation (`FUNCS_PER_CHUNK`), force `-O2` even in debug APKs, per-unit `-O1` overrides, exclude generated corpus from LTO (codepdbh battle scars).
2. `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` is a Play-policy liability — SAF + `getExternalFilesDir()` only. Never commit `local.properties` or personal toolchain paths (alexandercorp did both).
3. CPU affinity/priority tuning: pin **after** Vulkan device creation (driver threads), with SELinux-safe `/sys`-read fallback (some devices block cpufreq reads).
4. AAudio: underruns at unbounded target rates (codepdbh: 240 Hz target broke, 60 Hz clean); fade + error-callback restart; resampler on the game-thread-fed FIFO.
5. Present path: do real swapchain presentation; codepdbh's per-frame GPU→CPU `ANativeWindow_lock` readback is the known perf trap.
6. Adreno driver zips: ABI mismatch and malformed archives must fail closed; drivers live in app-private storage and are **user's third-party binaries** — never committed, never bundled in APKs.
7. Lifecycle: background/foreground swapchain recreation is an explicit gap in the reference projects — it is a test case for us (TC-9.4), not an afterthought.
8. Touch overlay UX lineage (reVC/reIII) is GPL-tainted — reimplement behavior descriptions, record inspiration as prose only.

### F. Gungnir-specific unknowns
1. `sceKernelLoadModule` usage (PPSSPP log) — which PRXs and when is discovered during T6; the overlay tier design must land before that, not after.
2. Engine script bytecode with absolute jumps is data, not code — but if any VM self-modifies or computes code pointers, the interpreter tier covers it (TC-5.4 counts those hits).
3. Dialog text = TPL font atlases with ink-width metrics (regenerating widths wrong causes collisions/clipping); UI text baked into TPL images needs image replacement, not font work — hence two-front text upscaling (T8).
4. TPL `bpp=5` CLUT layout is unmapped even in the ptbr tooling (grayscale only) — expected to matter little for text but must be decoded for correctness.
5. Audio decode quirk seen in PPSSPP logs (one reported error) — watch ATRAC edge cases in T12 soak tests.
6. Rumble: Gungnir's actual sceRumble-class usage is unknown until bring-up; haptics plumbing lands generic in T11, Gungnir mapping in T13/M5.
7. PPSSPP is the behavioral oracle (Perfect→Playable) — used for **diffing only, never linked or vendored** (sp00nznet's rule).

## 8. Cross-cutting test strategy

### 8.1 Red-first discipline (no regressions)

Every behavioral change follows the same loop, without exception:

1. **Red first.** The test (or fixture, gate, trace-assertion) lands *before* the implementation and is observed failing **for the expected reason** — a red run that fails for an unrelated error doesn't count. Commit the red test alongside the implementation it drives.
2. **Reproductions before fixes.** A bug fix starts with a test that reproduces the bug against current code (red), then the fix turns it green. This applies to bring-up bugs too: every `docs/BRINGUP.md` root-cause entry ends with a regression test name.
3. **No task closes red.** A task's test cases (TC-x.y) are its acceptance criteria; the task is done when they are green, and any test that must be disabled gets an itemized, time-boxed TODO — never a silent skip.
4. **Mutation checks gate semantic changes** (hst-decomp rule): for codegen/HLE changes, deliberately break one instruction/NID semantic and confirm the suite dies *for that reason* — mutations only count as evidence when they kill the gate correctly.
5. **Where red-first is not applicable:** pure research/spikes (e.g. Ghidra census tuning) and one-shot intake tooling (single known input) — but anything that touches runtime semantics, codegen, formats (DAR/TPL writers), or HLE behavior is red-first.

### 8.2 Oracle hierarchy & fixtures

1. **Oracle hierarchy:** our interpreter (in-repo truth) → synthetic golden traces (hand-computed expectations) → PPSSPP headless diff (optional, test-only) → on-device manual QA (see 8.3). Never link an emulator into the product.
2. **Synthetic-first:** every subsystem (decode, codegen, HLE, GE, TPL, DAR, SFO, input) has fixtures of **our own authorship** committed to `tests/fixtures/`; private game tests exist locally and `exit 77` in CI.
3. **Round-trip invariants:** every writer (DAR repack, TPL re-encode, font atlas repack, PARAM.SFO) must reproduce its input byte-identically before it may write anything new.
4. **Bounded runs everywhere** (azazel6): dispatch + wall-clock limits on any guest execution; synthetic runs are never reported as game runs; evidence labels (VERIFIED/HYPOTHESIS) in `docs/BRINGUP.md`.
5. **CI fail-closed:** tests needing game data skip with exit 77 (never pass silently); `repository_check` + secret scan + license gate are merge-blocking.

### 8.3 Manual QA on adb devices (mandatory)

Automated tests never close a device-facing milestone. Manual QA is a structured, recorded activity:

- **QA matrix per device-facing milestone (M4/M5):** at minimum one **Adreno** device (for driver-loader validation) and one **non-Adreno or handheld** device (Ayn/Ayaneo-class where possible) + the x86_64 emulator. Each cell records: device model, Android version, GPU/driver (system or custom zip + version), build ID (git SHA), date, tester.
- **Standard QA script** (`docs/QA.md`, kept current): cold boot to title; menu navigation via touch; menu navigation via gamepad (paired + built-in handheld controller); overlay hide-on-pad; suspend/resume (background/foreground) rendering recovery; rotation ignored; save/load if enabled; rumble feedback; audio smoke; 30-minute soak for crashes/thermal. T13 adds the Gungnir-specific script: title → menu → first gameplay transition.
- **Red-first applies to QA findings too:** a device bug becomes a reproducible case (steps, build, device) and, wherever host-testable, a red test before the fix.
- **Evidence:** QA reports live in `docs/qa/` (markdown, one file per session, dated) with **counts and pass/fail only** — no game screenshots in-repo; screenshot hashes recorded instead (images stay in gitignored `build/qa/`).
- **Sign-off:** M4 and M5 close only with an accepted QA report per device in the matrix. "Works on my machine once" is not evidence; "CI is green" is not evidence; three consecutive cold boots on each device are.

name: T8b — TPL writer and byte-identical round-trip
description:
Depends on: T8a.

Add a TPL writer that serialises the T8a decode model back to container
bytes: header, per-texture entries, swizzled texel data and CLUT tables.
Acceptance invariant (AGENTS.md writer rule, gungnir-ptbr proof #8): the
original fixture through decode -> encode must be byte-identical to the
input; any diff names the first mismatching offset. The writer must not
normalise padding, entry order or unused fields.

Cover re-encode at odd widths, multi-texture containers (n_tex > 1), 4bpp
swizzle and 8bpp CLUT. Byte-identity against the user's local TPLs is an
opt-in documented command, never CI and never a committed artifact.

Tests (red first):
- TC-8.1 encode half: synthetic decode -> encode is byte-identical, and the
  suite fails when a single header or swizzle byte is perturbed.
- Round-trip of every T8a edge-case fixture; mutation check: off-by-one BW
  or dropped CLUT entry must fail the identity check for that reason.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "tpl" --extension cpp`; `gh search code
"swizzle" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "TPL encode"`; `gh search
code "texture_replacement" --extension cpp`.

Refs: gungnir-ptbr round-trip discipline, psprecore texture decode inverse
behavior (MIT), existing T7 texture cache key tests for fixture style.
Gotchas: §7B.2-B.4.
result:
Added tex::write_tpl (TplWriteResult) as an in-place TPL writer. It starts from Tpl::bytes, rewrites the n_texture/table header, texture descriptors (H/W/BW/format/data offset), palette descriptors and texture/palette bytes at their recorded offsets, and preserves padding, raw auxiliary-resource headers, unknown tail bytes and the 8 opaque bytes in each texture descriptor. Unmodified decode -> write is byte-identical; edits to TplTexture::data or palette change exactly those bytes.

Validation fails closed with named errors: invalid_model, invalid_table_offset, invalid_texture_count, table_mismatch, entry_count_mismatch, truncated_header, truncated_entry_table, texture_header_out_of_range, unsupported_pixel_format, invalid_texture_dimensions, invalid_buffer_width, invalid_swizzle_geometry, data_size_mismatch, data_out_of_range, palette_header_out_of_range, invalid_palette_entries, unsupported_palette_format, palette_size_mismatch, palette_out_of_range, missing_palette, resource_header_out_of_range, resource_out_of_range.

Tests in tests/tex/tpl_tests.cpp: byte-identical round-trip for single/multi-texture, RGB565, CLUT8 and resource containers; single-byte texel and palette edits with all other bytes unchanged; rejected inconsistent models. Mutation check: replacing the writer body with 'return tpl.bytes' fails 'writer writes the modified texel'. Local ASan/UBSan validation round-tripped all 1,304 parseable user containers byte-identically (1,886 textures, 564 resources); debugFont.tpl remains the one named unsupported-format gap. Full suite 76/76 green; repository_check PASS (216 files).

description:

- Emit a build-time report naming every applied per-unit override.

result:
Android optimization: gungnir_add_runtime_library now adds -O2 -fno-lto to the shared target even in debug, and GUNGNIR_ANDROID_O1_SOURCES (passed by Gradle as -Pgungnir.o1Sources) applies a later -O1 to named sources. The clean-checkout test parses CMake compile_commands and verifies runtime TUs carry -O2/-fno-lto while the named vertex.cpp carries a later -O1.

Affinity: added runtime/platform/android/{affinity.hpp,affinity.cpp}. It parses Cpus_allowed_list ranges/singletons, reads /proc/self/status, chooses the highest allowed CPU, calls sched_setaffinity after Vulkan device creation, and requests nice -10 via setpriority. Missing status/list, invalid lists, affinity denial and priority denial are named; tuning never fails boot. Host tests inject the affinity/priority setters so they do not alter the test process.

Evidence: phone logged affinity_applied cpu=7 and priority_applied nice=-10; emulator logged affinity_applied cpu=3 and priority_applied nice=-10; both still rendered first frame. Full suite 103/103 green; repository_check PASS (264 files).

References used: plan §7E.1 (NDK Clang/generated TU optimization) and §7E.3 (affinity after Vulkan device creation, SELinux-safe fallback), codepdbh affinity/priority behavior (no code copied), Linux sched_setaffinity/setpriority and Android /proc/self/status Cpus_allowed_list semantics. name: T13j — Device process grows to multi-GB and is killed by low-memory
description:
The Android process is killed by the system for LOW_MEMORY on the new-game path: dumpsys activity exit-info reports reason=3 (LOW_MEMORY) with pss 3.4GB in a ~2 minute session (earlier title-only sessions reached 9.4GB). Guest RAM is 32 MiB and the corpus is ~100 MB, so something host-side retains memory per frame or per transition.

Reproduce with scripts/android/qa-newgame.sh (title -> NEW GAME -> difficulty -> ADVANCE -> confirm). Sample RSS/PSS with adb shell dumpsys meminfo com.gungnir.recomp during the run; capture logcat and exit-info into build/qa/android/ (gitignored).

Expectations: find the owner (presentation/frame queue, audio mixer, GE draw lists, screenshot buffers, or a guest-side leak surfaced through a host container), fix it, and prove it with a bounded host test where possible plus a device run that survives the new-game transition without LMK. This is a T13 engineering defect; T14 owns the formal QA matrix. Do not paper over it by raising memory limits or trimming frames silently.

## State 2026-11-01

**Reproduction.** `scripts/android/qa-newgame.sh` drives title -> NEW GAME ->
difficulty -> ADVANCE -> confirm on the M2102K1AC, then samples `Native Heap`
PSS every 2 s and reports `PROCESS_MEMORY_GROWTH` above `MEM_LIMIT_MB`
(default 2048), `PROCESS_KILLED` from `exit-info`, or `GUEST_FAULT`. Evidence
goes to gitignored `build/qa/android/t13i-newgame-<stamp>/` (screenshots,
`meminfo.txt`, `logcat.txt`, `exit-info.txt`).

**Measured.** The new-game path reaches the "Dept. Heaven Episode" prologue
with no guest fault, then the native heap reaches ~8.1 GB in roughly 30 s
(`Native Heap Pss Total 8156632 KB`, heap size 8.6 GB). Android kills the
process for `reason=3 (LOW_MEMORY)`; killed-session PSS was 3.4 GB in one run
and 9.4 GB in older title-only runs. Guest RAM is 32 MiB, so this is host-side
retention, not guest memory.

**Leading hypotheses.** Per-frame retention in the presentation/Vulkan path
(command buffers/descriptor pools/images), the GE draw/frame queue, or the
audio/mixer sink; a guest-side leak would still have to surface through a host
container. The title path already leaked before the new-game fix, so the
transition is an amplifier, not the origin.

**Next.** Profile native allocations across frames on the host/device (heap
profiler or ASan/LSan on a host reproduction), find the owning component, and
add a bounded regression (e.g. steady-state native allocation after N flips).
Fix and device-validate with `qa-newgame.sh` expecting `NEW_GAME_REACHED` with
a bounded PSS. Do not raise limits or drop frames silently.

## Root cause and fix (2026-11-01)

**Measured.** `qa-newgame.sh` with a corrected `Native Heap` parse (the older
script read column 2, `Heap`, so the growth check never ran): 8,022,869 KB of
native-heap PSS after ~1,140 guest frames (20 fps, 79 draws/frame), then
`reason=3 (LOW_MEMORY)`.

**Cause.** Three process-lifetime caches, all keyed by texture content hash:
`StateMachine::cpu_textures_` (raw guest bytes + `Texture`, appended per
textured draw and only cleared by `reset()`, which production never calls),
`TextureCache` (decoded RGBA pixels), and `VulkanBackend`'s `Impl::textures`
(one image/sampler/descriptor per key). Animated or CLUT-swapped content
changes the hash every frame, so each grew by ~6.6 MB/frame.

**Fix.** Draws now own `shared_ptr`s to their decoded image and source
texture, so queued frames keep what they sample while caches stay bounded:
`TextureCache` is an LRU with a 64 MiB byte budget; the GPU cache is an LRU
with 512-entry / 128 MiB limits. GPU eviction runs after the frame fence and
retired images are reaped at the next idle frame; `invalidate_texture` defers
destruction instead of blocking the guest thread.

**Prior art (reviewed after the first cut; the process miss is recorded in
`docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`).** PPSSPP `GPU/Common/TextureCacheCommon.cpp`
(`TextureCacheCommon::Decimate`, `TEXCACHE_MIN_PRESSURE` = 128 MiB,
`TEXTURE_KILL_AGE` = 200 / CLUT variants 6, `EstimateTexMemoryUsage`,
issue #10418) and psprecore `runtime/src/platform/gpu_vulkan.cpp`
(`evict_textures` after submit at `frame_number - last_frame > 240`, deferred
garbage in the frame slot). Both bound by age/size; neither retains decoded
textures for the process lifetime.

**Regressions.** `ge_state_machine_tests.bounded_texture_retention` (red at
399 entries / ~100 MB before the fix) and
`ge_vulkan_tests.bounded_gpu_texture_cache`; the state-machine binary is now
run by `tests/test_ge.py` (it was built but never executed).


## Device verification (2026-11-01)

APK `ce3a32a5c416f11f587dbef9e1b1f63a387a1b0f7afffc40f19372dc7ca84e58`
(debug, arm64-v8a, corpus `build/profile-test/generated`) installed on the
M2102K1AC. `scripts/android/qa-newgame.sh` (native-heap parse fixed) drove
title -> NEW GAME -> difficulty -> ADVANCE -> confirm and monitored 60 s.

**Result: `NEW_GAME_REACHED native_heap_pss_mb=186`.** Native-heap PSS stayed
180-182 MB for the first ~23 s (~1,400 guest frames), moved through a
168 -> 235 MB band during the prologue scene change (draws/frame rose from 79
to 272-280), then settled at 190 MB. Before the fix the same path reached
8,022,869 KB (~8.0 GB) at ~1,140 frames and was killed for `LOW_MEMORY`.
1620 guest frames in 60 s, no `Guest memory access` or `session_run_failed`.

Evidence (gitignored): `build/qa/android/t13i-newgame-20261031-232341/`
(`meminfo.txt`, `meminfo-final.txt`, `logcat.txt`, screenshots).


## Wrap-up 2026-11-01

- Host gates: full suite 170 OK (11 skipped); `repository_check` PASS (391
  files); `git diff --check` clean. New contracts:
  `bounded_texture_retention` (was red at 399 entries / ~100 MB) and
  `bounded_gpu_texture_cache`; the state-machine binary is now run by
  `tests/test_ge.py`.
- Device: APK `ce3a32a5c416f…`, `NEW_GAME_REACHED native_heap_pss_mb=186`,
  1,620 guest frames in 60 s, native heap 180-235 MB; pre-fix 8.0 GB at
  1,140 frames with `LOW_MEMORY`.
- References recorded in `docs/BRINGUP.md` and `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`
  (PPSSPP `TextureCacheCommon`, psprecore `evict_textures`; behavioural only).
- Changes are uncommitted; commit awaits user approval.
result:
Fixed the native-heap growth on the new-game path. Three process-lifetime caches were retaining texture payloads: StateMachine::cpu_textures_ (raw guest bytes + Texture, appended per textured draw and cleared only by reset(), which production never calls), TextureCache (decoded RGBA pixels), and VulkanBackend's Impl::textures (image/sampler/descriptor per content key). Animated and CLUT-swapped content changes the content hash every frame, so all three grew together (~6.6 MB/frame; 8.0 GB at 1,140 frames).

Fix: DrawState now holds shared_ptr owners for the decoded image and source bytes, so queued frames keep exactly what they sample; TextureCache is an LRU with a 64 MiB byte budget; the GPU cache is an LRU with 512-entry / 128 MiB limits, evicting after the frame fence with retired images reaped at the next idle frame; invalidate_texture defers destruction instead of blocking the guest thread.

Evidence: host suite 170 OK (11 skipped), repository_check PASS, git diff --check clean. New red-first contracts bounded_texture_retention (399 entries/~100 MB before the fix) and bounded_gpu_texture_cache; tests/test_ge.py now runs the state-machine binary. Device (M2102K1AC, APK ce3a32a5c416f…): qa-newgame.sh returns NEW_GAME_REACHED native_heap_pss_mb=186, 1,620 guest frames in 60 s, heap 180-235 MB; the pre-fix run died with LOW_MEMORY at 8.0 GB. description:

# T13a — Android runtime session: AOT corpus + HLE/audio/savedata in the APK

**Depends on:** none inside T13 (parent dependencies are complete).

**Goal.** The Android APK must run the same guest session as the Linux bounded boot: user-generated AOT corpus, `runtime/hle/*`, ATRAC decode, SAS/mixer and the virtual memstick. T13a ends at module init plus the first guest display flip (`cause=first_flip`); GE-list presentation and the title screen are T13b. Before this task `cmake/AndroidRuntime.cmake` compiled only the GE/input/audio-sink subset and the synthetic triangle entry point; `runtime/hle`, `runtime/audio/atrac_file.cpp`, `runtime/savedata` and `third_party/atrac3p` were absent.

**Work.**
- Factor the session core out of `tests/hle/boot_runner.cpp` into a shared, platform-neutral `runtime/session/` (module load, AOT registration, HLE registration, bounded dispatch + wall clock, stop cause, import/NID accounting, flip/dispatch counters, deterministic thread table). Make `boot_runner` and the Android entry point use the same code — no second boot implementation.
- Add HLE, `atrac_file`, savedata and `atrac3p` to `cmake/AndroidRuntime.cmake` (and the Android CMake source list), including include paths and `-O2 -fno-lto`; keep the per-unit `-O1` override working. Do not fork desktop sources.
- Add a local-only corpus input: `-Pgungnir.gameCorpus=DIR` (generated TUs + `manifest.json`) plus a synthetic-fixture mode for CI. Generated AOT code stays build output: never committed, never packaged as source, never in releases. The manifest path must be validated and a missing corpus must fail with a named CMake/Java error, not an empty runtime.
- Android session wiring: run the guest on its own thread; take the verified disc from `getExternalFilesDir()/game/`; mount the memstick at `getFilesDir()/psp/PSP/SAVEDATA` (T12b gap); load the packaged NID CSV; add bounded-run intent extras (dispatch limit, wall seconds) with safe defaults; emit one machine-readable `session_stop` log line with cause, dispatches, flips, imports bound/executed, missing and silent NID counts. Unknown NIDs keep trapping loudly.
- Extend `scripts/android/run.sh` (or a `--bounded` mode) to wait for the game-session line rather than only the synthetic `first frame`, with a named timeout; no sleeps that mask failure.
- Seed the Android memstick from user-pushed saves only (no bundled saves, no game data in the APK).

**Test cases (red-first).**
- `tests/android/session_tests.cpp` with a synthetic Allegrex fixture: bounded stop cause, dispatch/wall limits, deterministic two-run table, missing NID is a loud failure, no silent zero-return.
- `tests/test_android_runtime.py` (new): the Android CMake source list contains HLE/audio/savedata/atrac3p; `gameCorpus` absent fails with a named error; generated paths are not under the repo; no generated corpus is tracked.
- Extend `tests/test_android_build.py` to build the APK with the synthetic corpus (SDK-gated) and to assert the corpus property reaches CMake.
- Mutation check: break one session semantic (e.g. stop-cause classification or import accounting) and confirm the host suite dies for that reason.

**Acceptance / evidence.**
- Android boot with the user's local corpus reaches module init and the first guest display flip under explicit bounds; `run.sh` accepts only `session_stop cause=first_flip ... missing_import=0`; the executed-import set is disjoint from the unbound set. Screenshot evidence and title rendering belong to T13b.
- Synthetic-corpus APK builds with no game data present.
- `git ls-files` shows no generated AOT or game artifact; `repository_check` PASS.

**Guardrails.** AOT output is a derivative of the copyrighted executable — build output only. No game data, no screenshots, no dump hashes in tracked files. Bounded runs everywhere; no fake frame and no silent fallback. PPSSPP is a diff oracle, never linked. Do not reimplement the ATRAC parser or SFO writer — reuse the vendored code.

**Docs.** `docs/ANDROID.md` runtime-chain section, `docs/BRINGUP.md` entry for every blocker, `docs/TESTING.md` for the new host gate.

**Reference projects (patterns, not vendored code).**
- `AdamFull/ff7ccrecomp` (MIT) — Android Gradle/CMake wiring for a psprecore-style runtime, SDL3 Java integration, generated-output gitignore.
- `AdamFull/psprecore` (MIT) — platform-neutral frontend/session split and boot structure; never vendor its unlicensed `nx-foundation` subtree.

name: T9b — Shared runtime CMake, JNI bridge and SDL3 probe APK
description:

- `android/app/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt` defines a `gungnir_add_runtime_library()` function (`nk_add_title_runtime`-style) that compiles the same runtime sources for Android and desktop; no runtime fork and no duplicate source lists.

name: T8e — Font atlas repack tool and ink-width table
description:
Depends on: T8b.

Write tools/textures/repack_font_atlas.py: re-rasterize the dialog font atlas
at 2x/4x from a user-supplied glyph source, regenerate the ink-width advance
table, and repack through the T8b writer. The tool runs the identity gate
first and refuses to write unless the original atlas round-trips byte-
identically; text upscaling has two fronts, so this task covers atlases while
T8d image replacement covers baked-in UI text. No font files, glyphs or game
text are committed; the glyph source is user-supplied and gitignored.

Tests (red first):
- TC-8.3: a fixed synthetic test string at 2x and 4x renders without glyph
  collisions; regenerated width entries match hand-computed ink widths.
- Mutation check: an off-by-one advance entry fails the width assertion.
- Repack refuses on an identity failure and writes nothing.
- Round-trip: original atlas through the tool unchanged is byte-identical.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "font atlas" --extension cpp`; `gh search
code "ink width"`; `gh search code "pgf" --extension c`; `gh search issues
"font width"`.

Refs: gungnir-ptbr font metric facts and round-trip proof #8, sal063 pgf.c
parser (layout reference for future sceLibFont), T8b writer. Gotchas: §7F.3
(width collision, baked-in text), §7F.4.
result:
Added tools/textures/repack_font_atlas.py. It decodes a single-texture 4bpp PSP-swizzled font TPL with a 16-entry RGBA8888 palette, overlays user-supplied glyph bitmaps from JSON at base cell size, scales the atlas at 1-8x with nearest-neighbour replication, writes a new TPL and emits an ink-width table (atlas metadata plus per-cell left/right/width, optional code).

The identity gate decodes and re-encodes the original atlas before any write and aborts with identity_mismatch if the bytes differ; scale 1 with no glyphs is byte-identical. Glyph rows are validated against the cell shape and 0-15 values; invalid scale/input/geometry/cell cases write nothing. At scale 1, supplied glyphs change only atlas texels while preserving header/palette/tail; at Nx the header is rebuilt for scaled dimensions and the palette is preserved.

Tests in tests/test_font_repack.py (synthetic atlases only) cover identity, 2x/4x glyph and width scaling, a fixed three-glyph test string with no ink collisions, modified glyphs at scale 1, and malformed input/scale/cell refusals. Mutation: changing ink width to right-left+2 fails the width assertion. Local check: the real local dialog font round-tripped byte-identically through the identity gate and repacked to 832x512, which the TPL decoder/writer accepted. Full suite 83/83 green; repository_check PASS (229 files).

References used: gungnir-ptbr tools/fonte_gungnir.py (header/cell geometry and TPL decode/encode identity pattern), tools/acentos_gungnir.py (cell index formula, cell sizes 13x13 and 16x14, ink-width advance rule), tools/calib_largura.py (the game has no width table; advance is the glyph ink width), and the T8b writer/identity rule. No game font, glyph bitmap or translated text is committed; the glyph source is user-supplied.
