name: T13i — New-game initialisation: null object fault at guest 0x088FFF64
description:
Confirming a difficulty on the device faults inside guest code after a short run: 'Guest memory access outside PSP RAM/EDRAM at 0x00000020' at dispatch/PC 0x088FFF64. The getter at 0x088040A4 returns *(*(0x08A22EF4) + 0x5C), which is zero; the caller then calls 0x0881BC28 with a0=0 and the first access is this+0x20. Registers at the fault: a0=0 a1=8 a2=0 a3=0xBE sp=0x09FBF8E0 ra=0x088FFF70. Title screen, music, title menu and the difficulty selection all work (see docs/qa/2026-11-01-t13b-title.md); this is the new-game initialisation path. Start from a red-first host reproduction (the difficulty confirm needs injected pad input in the boot runner) or a guest call trace of the object at 0x08A22EF4, then fix the missing initialisation or the HLE call that should have created it. Do not paper over it with a null check.

## Progress 2026-11-01

**Host reproduction.** The boot runner now accepts repeatable
`--pad-press FLIP[:BUTTON[:HOLD]]` and applies the mask from a display-flip
observer, so menu paths can be driven deterministically on the host. The
sequence `--pad-press 460:cross:12 --pad-press 720:cross:12` reaches the
difficulty screen and confirms BASIC; it faults at `0x0880A8F8`
(`Guest memory access outside PSP RAM/EDRAM at 0x0`, a0=0). Selecting ADVANCE
(`--pad-press 700:down:8`) instead stops earlier at the unbound
`sceUtility::sceUtilityMsgDialogInitStart` (NID_0x2AD8E239).

**BASIC path diagnosis.** The caller at `0x0880A8F0` requests a 104-byte
object from the guest allocator at `0x08985BE8`; the allocator returns 0, the
caller branches to `0x0880A914` and dereferences the still-null pointer at
`gpr17+0` (`0x0880A918`/`0x0880A924`). The allocator normally returns
addresses inside the guest `UserSbrk` block (`0x08B38000`, size `0x19000`);
`PSPRECOMP_TRACE_PC=0x0880A8F8` shows ~1,900 successful returns followed by
the single zero, so this is an allocator failure, not an immediate sbrk
exhaustion. The game prints `POLL SEMA` just before the failure. The guest
FPL calls are present (`sceKernelTryAllocateFpl` 488 times) and our
implementation matches PPSSPP's success/`NO_MEMORY` contract, so the failing
request is the game's own heap/free-list path.

**Savedata gap.** With `GUNGNIR_TRACE_SAVEDATA=1` the boot calls savedata mode
**11 (LIST)** for `GUN9THSYS`, `GUN9THSTORY*` and `GUN9THCLEAR*`; our handler
returns `0x80110300` for it. That leaves the game's save-slot list
uninitialised before the new-game path and is the leading candidate for the
missing object.

**References used.**
- `hrydgard/ppsspp` `Core/HLE/sceKernelMemory.cpp` (`sceKernelTryAllocateFpl`
  success writes the block pointer and returns 0, failure returns
  `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_NO_MEMORY`) — matches our contract.
- `hrydgard/ppsspp` `Core/HLE/sceUtility.cpp`, `Core/Dialog/PSPMsgDialog.cpp`,
  `Core/Dialog/PSPDialog.cpp` — message-dialog init/update/get-status/
  shutdown state machine and the auto-acceptable button result.
- `snuri00/psp-web-recomp` `profile/host/devices.cpp` — a static-recomp
  message-dialog HLE that writes result 0 and `buttonPressed = YES`, plus
  FPL handling; behavioral reference only.
- `jpcsp/jpcsp` `src/jpcsp/HLE/modules/sceUtility.java` and
  `psplibdoc/modules150/sceUtility.java` — savedata/message-dialog semantics.
- `pspdev/pspsdk` `psputility_msgdialog.h`, `psputility_savedata.h` — struct
  layouts and mode names (LIST = 11).

**Next.** Implement the four `sceUtilityMsgDialog*` imports (headless
auto-accept, documented) and savedata LIST (empty list first, then real
entries), then rerun the two pad scripts. Both are already named gaps
(sceUtility dialogs and savedata LIST).

## Progress 2026-11-01 (dialog + LIST)

**Implemented.** The four `sceUtilityMsgDialog*` imports with a documented
headless auto-accept (result 0, `buttonPressed = 1`, V1/V2/V3 sizes), and
savedata mode 11 (LIST) filling `SceUtilitySavedataIdListInfo` from the save
directories matching `gameName + saveName` with `*`/`?` wildcards. Tests:
`utility_dialog_contracts` and the LIST block in `savedata_contracts`
(red-first; now green). Docs updated in `docs/HLE.md` and `docs/SAVEDATA.md`.

**Host runs.** ADVANCE no longer stops on the missing import: 2,000,000
dispatches, 9,199 flips, dispatch limit at `0x08805DEC`. The game then
retries savedata mode 4 (LISTLOAD) 613 times, so LISTLOAD is the next gap.
BASIC still faults at `0x0880A8F8` (104-byte allocator request returns 0);
the dialog was not the cause.

**Next.** Decide whether to implement LISTLOAD (empty list and first-entry
selection) or keep tracing the BASIC allocator failure.

## LISTLOAD research 2026-11-01

The title calls savedata mode 4 with `saveNameList = GUN9THSTORY00..31`,
`fileName = STORY`, `focus = 3` (LATEST); `idList` is set but unused.

- **PPSSPP** `SavedataParam::SetPspParam` reads the zero-terminated 20-byte
  `saveNameList`, keeps only existing save directories (`listEmptyFile =
  false`), expands `"<>"` to every game-prefixed directory, and falls back to
  the single `gameName + saveName` when no list is usable. `PSPSaveDialog`
  shows NODATA for zero candidates; cancel sets
  `SCE_UTILITY_SAVEDATA_ERROR_LOAD_NO_DATA` (0x80110307). `focus` selects via
  FirstList/LastList/Latest/Oldest/FirstData/LastData (unknown and FirstList =
  index 0); LATEST/OLDEST compare the `PARAM.SFO` mtime. `LoadSaveData`
  writes the selected name back to `saveName`, then the LOAD path sets
  `bind = 1021`, `dataSize`, SFO fields and icons.
- **JPCSP** `MODE_LISTLOAD` iterates `saveNameList` with `isPresent()` and
  returns `ERROR_SAVEDATA_LOAD_NO_DATA` when the list is empty; on OK it sets
  `saveName = saveListSelection` and loads.
- **PSPSDK sample** (`src/samples/savedata/utility/main.c`) drives the same
  status loop and fills `saveNameList` before InitStart.

Proposed headless policy: empty list auto-cancels with 0x80110307; a
non-empty list auto-selects the `focus` entry and runs the LOAD, writing the
selected name back. Research recorded in `docs/BRINGUP.md`.

**Next action.** Implement mode 4 (LISTLOAD) with that headless policy:
`saveNameList` candidates (existing dirs only, `"<>"` expansion, single-save
fallback), focus-based selection, `0x80110307` on an empty list, selected
name written back, then the normal LOAD path (`bind = 1021`, `dataSize`,
SFO/icons). Red-first tests for exact/wildcard/empty/fallback/focus cases;
rerun the ADVANCE pad script and confirm the mode-4 retry loop stops.

## Progress 2026-11-01 (LISTLOAD)

Mode 4 is implemented with the researched headless policy: candidates from
the zero-terminated `saveNameList` (existing directories only, `"<>"`
expansion, single-save fallback), `focus` selection (first/last/latest/
oldest/first-data/last-data), `0x80110307` for an empty list, selected name
written back, then the normal LOAD path. `savedata_listload_contracts` was
red-first and is now green; `docs/SAVEDATA.md`, `docs/HLE.md` and
`docs/BRINGUP.md` updated.

**Host result.** ADVANCE no longer retries mode 4. It reaches the new-game
setup and faults on an indirect call to address 0 at `0x0880602C`
(`ctx.pc = gpr6`, `gpr6 = [gpr7 + 4] = 0`; reported at dispatch `0x08806034`
with `guest_pc=0x08838A44`). BASIC still faults at `0x0880A8F8` when a
104-byte allocator request returns 0. No HLE import is unbound; both are
guest-side null objects, likely one root cause.

**Next.** Trace the shared null-object/allocator failure (BASIC
`0x0880A8F8`, ADVANCE `0x0880602C`) rather than adding more save modes.

## Null-object trace 2026-11-01

**BASIC.** The 104-byte allocation fails deterministically at call 1969 on a
fresh memory stick. The game's heap descriptor is `0x08ACF3A8`; the same
112-byte chunk is reused ~1,006 times, and the last successes reach
`0x08B40030` inside the 0x19000 `UserSbrk` block, leaving ~69 KB unused when
the allocator gives up. The chain is guest code
`0x08985BE8` -> `0x08973094` -> `0x08977F4C`; no HLE allocator is involved.
Likely free-list corruption/fragmentation in the game's heap.

**ADVANCE.** gdb catch-throw shows the fatal path is
`GuestMemory::load8` <- `aot_load32_slow` <- `recomp_unit_0101_entry` at
guest `0x0899B3F0`, a routine that copies VFPU 4x4 matrices from a source
pointer; the caller passes a null source. No missing import or HLE handler
appears in the throw. After LISTLOAD returns `NO_DATA` there are no further
savedata requests; the last I/O is the story `data.dar` reads and an async
open of `bgm/bgm01.at3`.

**Next.** Trace the HLE calls in the transition window and compare with
PPSSPP, then find the guest factory that should populate the matrix source /
the heap corruption source. Diagnostics were temporary and have been
reverted.

## HLE call ring 2026-11-01

Added `GUNGNIR_HLE_RING=N`: the registrar wraps bound imports, keeps the last
N calls (`a0`-`a3`, `v0`/`v1`, return PC, thread) and the session prints the
ring on a fault. In ADVANCE the window before the null matrix copy contains
only ordinary calls (`sceRtcGetCurrentTick`, `sceKernelDcacheWritebackRange`
size 0, `sceKernelCheckCallback` = 0, `sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking` = 0). In
BASIC the allocator's `sceKernelCpuSuspendIntr`/`ResumeIntr` bracket the heap,
then the same audio call precedes the failed 104-byte request. No HLE return
is visibly wrong; the next step is guest-state tracing (the matrix source
factory and the heap free-list corruption).

## Checkpoint 2026-11-01

Committed as `4800976` ("Add message-dialog HLE and savedata list modes"):
message-dialog HLE, savedata LIST and LISTLOAD, pad-press harness, HLE call
ring, PollSema trace, tests and docs, plus the T14 split. Full suite 169 OK
(11 skipped), `repository_check` PASS.

**Current state.** The title, music, menu and difficulty selection work on
the M2102K1AC device. Both host new-game paths still die in guest code:

- BASIC: the game's own allocator returns 0 for a 104-byte request at guest
  call 1969 (`0x0880A8F8`); ~69 KB of the 0x19000 `UserSbrk` block is unused,
  so this is free-list corruption/fragmentation, not exhaustion.
- ADVANCE: after LISTLOAD returns `NO_DATA`, translated code at
  `0x0899B3F0` copies VFPU matrices from a null source; the indirect call at
  `0x0880602C` reads a null `[gpr7+4]` dispatch entry.

No missing import and no visibly wrong HLE return in either window.

**Next step (before code changes).** Collect references and instrumentation
for guest-state tracing: the last translated PCs/registers before each fault,
the factory that should populate the matrix source and the dispatch table
slot, and the game heap free-list at the 1969th allocation. Compare the
transition window with PPSSPP/psprecore behaviour where the same engine is
observable, and check the disc-read trace for short/zero reads that would
leave asset records zeroed.

## Research 2026-11-01 (instrumentation + call site)

**Correction.** The ADVANCE fault is *not* an indirect call to address 0 at
`0x0880602C`; `0x08806034` is the return PC from that call. The callee is a
descriptor-dispatched thunk, and `0x08838A44` copies a matrix with
`src = a2 = 0`. The earlier note in this description overstated the call-site
finding.

**Diagnostics.** `PSPRECOMP_TRACE_ON_ERROR` already records 64 outer
dispatches; `set_runtime_pre/post_chained_call_hook` observes dynamic
`invoke_chained_call` targets but not compile-time
`invoke_chained_direct<...>`. Because the fault is deep inside one outer
dispatch, the existing rings cannot show the caller of `0x08838A44`.

**Call site / table.** `0x0880602C` loads `desc = [object + 248]`, adds the
s16 `this` adjustment at `desc + 0`, and calls `[desc + 4]`. The static
descriptor table is 116 `{u32 offset, u32 fn}` entries at `0x08AD0B7C`; the
`0x08838A44` descriptor is at `0x08AD0DE0`. `0x08838A44` is
`copy(dest = a1, src = a2)` through `0x0899B3F0` (four VFPU vectors).
`0x08838A40` is the delay slot of the preceding `jr $ra`, so the function
seed recorded there by the analyzer is spurious.

**Basic allocator.** The 104-byte request is a C++ `new`; the constructor at
`0x088104F8` writes vtable `0x08AD0308` at `object + 100`. The game's own
allocator (its `faile[%s]:%dbyte Allocation(rest[%d])` diagnostic) fails while
~69 KB remains, and the ring shows a successful 112-byte request immediately
before. Allocator state at `0x08ACF3A8` has 0x58-byte-spaced small-bin heads.
HYPOTHESIS: size-class/free-list bookkeeping or chunk-header corruption.

**References.** PPSSPP `sceKernelInterrupt.cpp` (Suspend/ResumeIntr returns
and restores the previous state; bit 0 on resume) matches our handler;
PPSSPP runs Gungnir (open issues are texture sampling `#15449` and an old
battle crash `#4446`); no decompilation/symbol source exists for the title.

**Next.** Build a dynamic chained-call ring (target, depth, a0-a3) filtered
around `0x08838A44` to get its caller and the null source, and/or a
dispatch-boundary guard on `0x08ACF3A8`..`0x08ACF700` to find the first
foreign write to the allocator header. Both are opt-in diagnostics; the
reproduction is already deterministic.

Research recorded in `docs/BRINGUP.md`.

## Root cause found 2026-11-01

Added a dynamic chained-call ring (`GUNGNIR_CHAIN_RING=N`, session diagnostics)
and documented the existing guest write watch as the heap guard
(`PSPRECOMP_WATCH_WRITE`/`_SIZE`). The ring showed the null matrix source was
already zero when `0x08834804` was called, and that the thread switch happened
inside `sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking`.

**Bug.** `hle_audio.cpp` called `kernel().finish(ctx, enqueue_blocking(...))`.
`enqueue_blocking` parks the caller and may switch threads; `finish` then wrote
the audio result into the new thread's context, zeroing the resumed thread's
`v0` and producing the null matrix pointer.

**Fix.** Capture the execution-context token before the blocking call and call
`finish` only if the same thread is still current; `block` already records the
parked thread's result. Red-first contract in `audio_contracts` sets a sentinel
in the parked loader's `v0` and failed before the fix ("blocking output must
not clobber the resumed thread's result").

**Host.** Both paths survive the former faults. ADVANCE: 1,500,000
dispatches, 6,965 flips, dispatch limit at `0x08805DEC`. BASIC: 1,500,000
dispatches, 6,665 flips, dispatch limit at `0x0883AAC0` (the old 1969th
allocation failure is gone). References: PPSSPP
`sceAudio.cpp` (blocking output returns to the parked thread) and the
session/thread contracts.

**Next.** Confirm BASIC, run the full suite, then commit the diagnostics + fix.

## Verification 2026-11-01

- Red-first audio contract failed before the fix and passes after it.
- Full suite: 169 tests OK (11 skipped).
- Android cross-compile: `cmake/AndroidRuntime.cmake` also compiles
  `runtime/session/diagnostics.cpp`; the wiring contract in
  `tests/test_session.py` covers it.
- ADVANCE (1.5M): 6,965 flips, dispatch limit at `0x08805DEC`.
- BASIC (1.5M): 6,665 flips, dispatch limit at `0x0883AAC0`; the former 1969th
  allocation failure is gone.
- `repository_check` PASS; `git diff --check` clean. Changes are uncommitted.
- 2,000,000-dispatch ADVANCE with savedata tracing: 9,335 flips, dispatch
  limit at `0x0883B190`, no fault and no savedata request after the empty
  LISTLOAD. Host evidence stops at "the old fault is gone"; whether the new
  game reaches gameplay is a T14 device check, not a host claim.

## Device QA 2026-11-01

APK `0f2b4d19968464001da58672b2703a26dd007b614a7c487fb496d1a45bcfaa6e`
(debug, arm64-v8a, corpus `build/profile-test/generated`) installed on the
M2102K1AC (serial `30c1f958`). Driven with touch: NEW GAME at the title,
difficulty screen, d-pad down to ADVANCE, confirm.

**Result.** The former `0x088FFF64` null-object fault is **gone**. After the
ADVANCE confirm the game reaches the "Developed by STING" / "Dept. Heaven
Episode" new-game transition with `draws=79 vertices=414` and no
`Guest memory access` or `session_run_failed` log line.

**New blocker (T13j).** The process is then killed by Android for
`LOW_MEMORY`: `dumpsys meminfo` reports `Native Heap Pss Total 8156632 KB`
(~8.1 GB) about 30 s after launch; `exit-info` shows `reason=3 (LOW_MEMORY)`.
The new-game path itself is validated up to the prologue; full gameplay is
blocked by the host-side memory growth, not by guest code.

Evidence (gitignored): `build/qa/android/t13i-newgame-*/` with title,
difficulty, ADVANCE-selection, prologue screenshots, logcat and exit-info.
Reproduction: `scripts/android/qa-newgame.sh`.

## T13j cleared — gameplay validation remains (2026-11-01)

The host-side LOW_MEMORY blocker is fixed (`crfi1uug`). The rebuilt APK
(`ce3a32a5c416f…`) runs the same title -> NEW GAME -> difficulty -> ADVANCE ->
confirm path and reaches the "Dept. Heaven Episode" prologue with no
`Guest memory access`/`session_run_failed`: 1,620 guest frames in 60 s,
native-heap PSS 180-235 MB (pre-fix: 8.0 GB and a LOW_MEMORY kill at ~1,140
frames). Evidence: `build/qa/android/t13i-newgame-20261031-232341/`.

Remaining for this task: drive past the prologue into actual gameplay
(menus/battle/scripted scenes) on the device, record any new HLE gaps as named
failures with regressions, and close the device checklist. The former
`0x088FFF64` null-object fault is gone; the audio token fix and savedata

name: T10c — ICD loader shim and runtime Vulkan dispatch
description:
Depends on: T10a, T10b.

Add `runtime/platform/adreno/loader.{hpp,cpp}` and switch the Vulkan backend to runtime dispatch; `runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp` currently links `Vulkan::Vulkan` directly.
- System path: `dlopen` `libvulkan.so`/`vulkan-1` with the existing name list; the default selection never calls libadrenotools.
- Custom path: `adrenotools_open_libvulkan(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL, ADRENOTOOLS_DRIVER_CUSTOM, tmpLibDir, hookLibDir=nativeLibraryDir, customDriverDir=staged private dir, soname, fileRedirectDir, nullptr)` using T10b's package; fetch `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` and resolve instance/device entry points through it (volk-style table or a minimal own table; record the choice).
- Selection state: "system" default; selecting a driver loads once; failure returns a named error and the caller falls back to system without a partial instance. Desktop keeps the direct-link path.
- Version reporting: `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion` + `VK_KHR_driver_properties` (`driverName`/`driverInfo`) for the UI and one logcat line.

Tests (red first, host where possible): an injected opener seam proves the system path never calls the custom opener; custom success yields a usable function table; a null handle fails closed with a named error; no selection means system; a Vulkan fixture still renders through the dispatch table. A desktop build without libadrenotools stays green.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "adrenotools_open_libvulkan" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "vkGetInstanceProcAddr" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "custom Vulkan driver vkGetInstanceProcAddr"`; `gh search code "VK_KHR_driver_properties"`.

Refs: PPSSPP `Common/GPU/Vulkan/VulkanLoader.cpp`, Flycast/Dolphin/Vita3K call sites, libadrenotools `driver.h` (BSD-2), the current T7e backend. Gotchas: §7E.6.
result:
Added runtime/platform/adreno/loader.{hpp,cpp} with VulkanDriverSelection, VulkanDriverInfo and injectable system/custom/close hooks. System selection (the default) tries libvulkan.so.1 then libvulkan.so (vulkan-1.dll on Windows, MoltenVK names on macOS) and never calls the custom opener. Custom selection validates the private driver dir/soname/hook dir, calls adrenotools_open_libvulkan(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL, ADRENOTOOLS_DRIVER_CUSTOM, tmpLibDir, hookLibDir, customDriverDir, soname, nullptr, nullptr), and uses the returned vkGetInstanceProcAddr. Custom failures retain driver_load_failed or driver_abi_unsupported and fall back to system before any instance exists; the caller logs driver_fallback and boots.

Android arm64 compiles the vendored Volk table (commit aa76c86a, MIT) and calls volkLoadInstance/volkLoadDevice; desktop keeps the direct Vulkan link. The backend now exposes VulkanDriverInfo, queries VK_KHR_driver_properties when present (falling back to deviceName), and main logs driver_active=<system|custom> name=... info=... api=.... x86_64 builds have GUNGNIR_HAVE_ADRENOTOOLS=0, include no adrenotools symbols, and report driver_abi_unsupported for a custom selection.

Build: cmake/AdrenotoolsDeps.cmake fetches/libadrenotools and liblinkernsbypass from pinned commit archives, verifies SHA-256, composes the submodule at lib/linkernsbypass, and caches under build/android-deps. build.sh runs it; Gradle passes the source dirs. The APK packages libmain_hook.so, libfile_redirect_hook.so, libgsl_alloc_hook.so and libhook_impl.so for arm64 only, with useLegacyPackaging=true; no driver zip/.so is bundled.

Tests: tests/test_vulkan_loader.py runs injected-loader contracts (system path never calls custom, name ordering, custom success forwarding, fallback for null handle/missing entry point/missing ABI/invalid selection, total failure, close once); tests/ge/vulkan_tests.cpp asserts driver_info().loaded/name/api_version; tests/test_android_app.py pins the adrenotools/volk build wiring; tests/test_android_build.py asserts the arm64 hooks and no x86_64 hooks. Mutation: making the loader accept a null custom entry point kills 'missing entry point is named'. Emulator evidence: driver_active=system name=gfxstream (SwiftShader driver) info=Mesa 26.2.0-devel api=4206592, then first frame 640x320. The arm64 phone was not connected at this checkpoint; custom-driver device QA is T10e. Full suite 117/117 green; repository_check PASS (294 files); deps.py verify passes all nine entries.

References used: gh search code "volkInitializeCustom" --extension cpp (taichi/taichi vulkan_loader.cpp and other call sites); gh search code "VK_KHR_driver_properties" --extension cpp (PCSX2 GSDeviceVK.cpp, DuckStation vulkan_device.cpp, Skia); gh search issues "custom Vulkan driver vkGetInstanceProcAddr"; gh search code "adrenotools_open_libvulkan" --extension cpp (PPSSPP VulkanLoader.cpp, Dolphin VulkanLoader.cpp, Vita3K android_driver.cpp, Flycast adreno.cpp, Azahar native.cpp); libadrenotools include/adrenotools/driver.h and priv.h. Gotchas: plan §7E.6-E.7.

name: T11a — Input core and sceCtrl mapping
description:
Depends on: T9 (T6 for the existing sceCtrl surface). Parent T11.

Input foundation:
- Add `runtime/input/` with a source-neutral event/state model: button identity, press/release edges, analog X/Y, source (touch/gamepad/keyboard/mouse), pointer/device id.
- Feed the state into the existing sceCtrl surface: PSP button bits, analog stick, deadzone, [-128,127] clamp, pressed/edge semantics, and release-all on focus/background.
- Desktop keyboard/mouse fallback: a configurable map for d-pad, face buttons, L/R, START/SELECT and mouse buttons. This path is for desktop development only.
- Define and test a deterministic source-merge policy (for example, each button records its active sources; analog values are clamped after merge). Document the chosen policy.
- Keep the core free of Android/JNI/SDL dependencies so it is host-testable.
- Host unit tests: mapping table, deadzone/clamp, press/release edges, simultaneous sources, focus-loss release-all, unknown event no-op, deterministic merge.
- No touch overlay, haptics, gamepad profiles or remap UI in this subtask.

Reference set: Yakumo's MIT `input/touch_*`, `input/gamepad_mapping` and `bindings` are the primary mapping/semantics reference; PPSSPP's sceCtrl mapping is behavioral only (GPL, no code copied).

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): tests observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "sceCtrl" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "SceCtrlData" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "sceCtrl analog deadzone"`; `gh search code "input mapping" "PSP" --extension cpp`.
result:
T11a complete (commit bd2d954).

- runtime/input: source-neutral slots keyed by (source, device, pointer). Buttons OR across sources; analog uses the highest-priority engaged slot (Touch, Gamepad, Keyboard, Mouse), latest pointer per source; axes clamp to [-1,1] then apply the 0.12 dead zone; make/break edges are single-consumer. No SDL/JNI/guest-memory dependency.
- sceCtrl: Read/PeekBufferPositive publish the merged pad (buttons + both sticks) and sample the make/break/press/release latch; Read/PeekLatch registered. Latch sampling point is the positive-buffer read (guest frame loop), documented in the handler.
- Desktop fallback: KeyboardMap defaults (WASD/arrows, J/K/L/I, Q/E, Return/Backspace, mouse 1-3) plus an SDL3 adapter wired into the app loop; focus loss/background releases held keys and all input.
- Red-first: tests/input/input_tests.cpp and tests/test_input.py written before runtime/input existed; first build failed on the missing input_state.cpp, then contracts went green. media_tests gained live-pad and latch contracts. Deliberate mutation (pressed edges ORed every refresh) failed "holding does not repeat the edge"; reverted.
- Gates: full suite 134/134 OK; repository_check PASS (310 files); Android clean-checkout APK test and bounded boot test link/copy the new archive.

References: TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, pinned b61852a) input/touch_controls.hpp, gamepad_mapping.hpp and bindings.hpp for source/merge terminology only (no code copied); PPSSPP Core/HLE/sceCtrl.cpp for latch make/break/press/release semantics (behavioral only, GPL, no code copied); SDL3 scancode values checked by static_assert; docs/HLE.md updated for the new sceCtrl surface.

name: T6l — ATRAC track parse, decode and streaming
description:

When the boot executes them, add sceAtracSetData/SetDataAndGetID/SetHalfwayBuffer(AndGetID), GetSoundSample, GetChannel, GetMaxSample, GetRemainFrame, GetNextSample, DecodeData, SetLoopNum/GetLoopStatus, Release, GetBitrate, GetNextDecodePosition, ResetPlayPosition, GetStreamDataInfo/AddStreamData, SecondBuffer and BufferInfo APIs — RIFF/WAVE parse (AT3 fmt 0x270, AT3+ 0xFFFE, fact/smpl), loop points, guest PCM output, fail-closed errors; no fake PCM. Private local verification against a user AT3 with ffmpeg as oracle. Blocked by T6i.

ABI cross-check (2026-10-30): Zig-PSP's generated
`src/c/module/sceAtrac3plus.zig` and `src/sdk/atrac3.zig` (MIT) mirror PSPSDK
signatures, structs and error codes for the track APIs. Use them to
cross-check T6l's contracts; they contain no decoder.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

The FFmpeg n4.4 decoder is vendored and self-tested (4,149 checks); the handlers move to T12/M5 when the title starts decoding audio, and must never fake PCM.

name: T13b — Title screen and menu on device: 1x textures/text, 59.94 Hz pacing, touch + gamepad
description:
Part of T13 (plan §5, milestone M4). Owns the visual/input half of TC-13.1 on the emulator first; physical-device sign-off is T13f.

# T13b — Title screen and menu on device

**Depends on:** T13a.

**Goal.** Move from "a real game frame is presented" to "the Gungnir title screen is readable and the title menu responds to both input paths".

**Work.**
- Present guest GE output through the existing Android Vulkan swapchain at 1x: correct viewport/orientation, no unintended scaling, texture replacement loader active at 1x, text/font rendering visible. No game assets or frames in the repository.
- Implement 59.94 Hz pacing (frame = 16,683.35 µs) for `sceDisplay` VBlank and presentation, replacing the T12a pacing gap. Account for late frames explicitly (counted, no hidden sleep catch-up); expose frame time and vblank counters in the `session_stop`/periodic log.
- Verify the title screen's textures and text through the T8 replacement path at 1x. Fix rendering defects red-first; where host-testable, add a synthetic GE/texture fixture. Keep the software rasterizer as the parity oracle.
- Drive the title menu with the touch overlay and with a gamepad; verify overlay hide-on-pad, merged input into `sceCtrl`, and the title → menu → first gameplay transition. Use adb/SDL input injection, never xdotool.
- Capture a screenshot through `scripts/android/screenshot.sh`, record its SHA-256 and viewport/pacing measurements in a gitignored local milestone report. No image or hash of game content is committed; the public ledger gets counts/criteria only.
- Log zero unknown/silent NIDs at the deepest bounded run and classify every remaining gap in `docs/HLE.md`.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- `tests/ge` or a new pacing fixture: fake monotonic clock produces exact 16,683.35 µs vblank spacing, bounded catch-up, and a deliberately wrong period fails. Mutation check required.
- Synthetic title/text fixture renders through the replacement path at 1x with a pinned screenshot hash (our fixture, not game content).
- On-emulator manual evidence: title screen, touch menu navigation, gamepad menu navigation, overlay hide-on-pad, title → first gameplay transition, screenshot hash.
- Bounded-run log check: `session_stop` with `missing=0 silent=0` and a named stop cause.

**Acceptance / evidence.**
- Emulator title screen is readable at 1x and both input paths reach the first gameplay transition.
- Pacing measured and documented; no underrun or frame-pacing regression in the audio path.
- All findings recorded in `docs/BRINGUP.md` with a regression test or a tracked open defect.

**Guardrails.** Emulator evidence is bring-up, not milestone closure. No game screenshots, hashes of game files or dump identities in tracked files. No xdotool. No emulator code linked.

**Docs.** `docs/BRINGUP.md`, `docs/RENDERER.md` (1x/replacement notes), `docs/INPUT.md` (title-menu results), `docs/HLE.md` (gap table).

**Reference projects (oracles and UX patterns).**
- `hrydgard/ppsspp` (GPL-2.0-or-later) — `sceDisplay`/flip timing, texture-replacement and `textures.ini` semantics; diff oracle only, never linked.
- `BasedYuki/the-3rd-birthday-recomp` (GPL-2.0-or-later, PPSSPP-derived runtime) — `tools/pace_test.py` and the screenshot/compare harness; tooling may run out-of-tree, no code vendored.
- `AdamFull/psprecore` (MIT) — frontend/pause-overlay/menu structure and renderer parity shape.
- `AdamFull/ff7ccrecomp` (MIT) — texture replacement and recordings/replays UX.
- `TeamGDB/Yakumo` (MIT) — Android frontend/overlay behavior and Vulkan texture-cache handling as a cross-check.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Read the matching source with `gh repo read-file` / `gh repo read-dir`, never raw.githubusercontent.com. Record the references used in the task result; if a reference shapes the design, add a prose note to `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).
Specific first searches: `sceDisplaySetFrameBuf`, `sceDisplayWaitVblankStart`, `sceGeListEnQueue` flip semantics, `textures.ini` replacement rules; `gh search code "16683" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues "59.94 Hz pacing"` and `"frame pacing Adreno"`; 3rd Birthday `tools/pace_test.py` and psprecore overlay/frontend as behavioral references. `gh search code "SCREENSHOT_HASH"` is not useful here — use our own script and hash policy.

## Progress 2026-10-31 (in progress)

**Implemented.**
- `runtime/ge/state_machine.*`: GE register/matrix/texture state, vertex decode (through and 3D), matrices/viewport, texture decode with CLUT, scissor/blend/depth/cull, triangle/strip/fan and through/non-through sprite triangulation, named gaps for alpha test, mip levels and unsupported primitives. `runtime/ge/frame_queue.*` hands the latest frame to the present thread.
- `hle_media`: every decoded GE command now feeds the state machine; draws accumulate per list and are delivered on a real `sceDisplaySetFrameBuf` flip. Gaps are counted and each kind is logged once.
- `VulkanBackend::render_swapchain_draws`: presents guest draws to the swapchain (separate pipeline cache; empty call list clears without the synthetic triangle).
- `boot_runner --frame-json/--frame-at/--frame-ppm`: dumps a frame summary and renders the captured frame with the software rasterizer for parity.
- Android entry: continuous session (`stop_at_flip=false`, pacing on), frame queue, guest-frame logging, AAudio/mixer path retained.
- Tests: `tests/ge/state_machine_tests.cpp`, `tests/test_boot.py::test_first_flip_carries_guest_geometry` (frame 60), `tests/test_session.py` still green.

**Evidence so far.**
- Host: state-machine tests OK; real frame 60 has 31 draws / 3,924 vertices / 5,796 indices, 18 textured draws, textures 512x256; software rasterization shows the gold banner and text.
- Device: session runs at ~59.94 Hz with 31 draws/frame; no session stop, no crash. `ge_gaps` ~30/frame, currently `texture_mip_levels` and `alpha_test_unsupported` (and previously `sprite_non_through`, fixed).
- Device Vulkan output is wrong: a synthetic debug quad `(0,0)-(480,272)` renders as a small rainbow rectangle at the bottom-left, ~480/3063 of the surface width.

**Root cause found.**
`runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.cpp:1721-1722` in `recreate_swapchain()` overwrites `impl_->config.width/height` with the window/swapchain size (3063x1335). `render_swapchain_draws` uses `config.width/height` for the mesh shader's virtual coordinate space, so guest 480x272 geometry is squeezed into the bottom-left. The guest virtual size must be separate from the swapchain extent and must not be changed by resize.

**Next.**
1. Add dedicated `virtual_width/height` (default 480x272) to `VulkanBackend`; keep `config.width/height`/swapchain extent for the surface. Use virtual size for push constants; swapchain extent for viewport/scissor.
2. Verify debug quad fills the surface, then the title frame.
3. Fix the software-visible garbled text (texture/UV mapping) and alpha-test/mip gaps as needed.
4. Run touch and gamepad menu navigation, capture hashed evidence, update docs.

**Files.** `runtime/ge/state_machine.{hpp,cpp}`, `runtime/ge/frame_queue.{hpp,cpp}`, `runtime/hle/hle_media.{hpp,cpp}`, `runtime/ge/vulkan_backend.{hpp,cpp}`, `android/app/src/main/cpp/main.cpp`, `tests/ge/state_machine_tests.cpp`, `tests/hle/boot_runner.cpp`, `tests/test_boot.py`, `cmake/AndroidRuntime.cmake`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `docs/BRINGUP.md` (pending final entry).

## Progress 2026-11-01 (T13b continued)

**Presentation fixed (verified on device).**
- Guest virtual extent is now separate from the swapchain extent: `Config::virtual_width/height` (480x272) feed the mesh shader push constants, while viewport/scissor use the fitted swapchain rect. `recreate_swapchain()` no longer overwrites the guest size. `fit_viewport()` and `scale_scissor_to_extent()` carry unit tests (host `ge_vulkan_tests`).
- Android surface measures 3063x1335 with `currentTransform=ROTATE_90`. The swapchain now requests `preTransform=IDENTITY` and lets the compositor rotate; `VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR` on acquire/present is treated as success (Granite's Android policy). Previously the quad/title appeared rotated 90 degrees and squeezed into the bottom-left.
- A new frame is presented only when the frame queue has one; the swapchain is no longer cleared while waiting, which removed the black flicker between guest flips.
- Sprite expansion bug found and fixed: the bottom-left sprite vertex kept the top-left Y, so every sprite drew as a triangle. This was the garbled title text. Regression test `through_sprite_quad` in `tests/ge/state_machine_tests.cpp`. Text now renders legibly ("Checking storage media. Do not remove storage media.", publisher logo).

**Boot flow advanced to the title.**
- Savedata: after shutdown, `sceUtilitySavedataGetStatus` keeps returning 0 (NONE) instead of `WRONG_TYPE`, matching JPCSP's documented behavior; added a `started` flag. AUTOLOAD (mode 0) and AUTOSAVE (mode 1) are wired to the existing load/save paths. Kernel savedata tests extended.
- UMD: bound `sceUmdCheckMedium`, `sceUmdWaitDriveStat`, `sceUmdWaitDriveStatCB`, `sceUmdCancelWaitDriveStat`; the game stopped at `sceUmdCancelWaitDriveStat` before this.
- sceMpeg is deferred to T12/M5. All 38 sceMpeg entry points in the NID table (24 imported by this module) are now bound to explicit named-gap errors (`sceMpegInit` -> `SCE_MPEG_ERROR_NO_RAPI`, others -> `NOT_INITIALIZE`, cleanup returns success), logged as `[hle] gap: sceMpeg::...`. Without this the game skipped movies by stopping on a missing NID; with it the opening movie is skipped and boot continues.
- Scheduler fairness: after the MPEG failure the movie worker (`loopHacker`, priority 31) busy-polled `sceKernelTryReceiveMsgPipe`/`sceKernelCheckCallback` and starved `user_main` (priority 32). A provisional 50 us idle delay in `sceKernelCheckCallback` (no callbacks queued) lets the main thread run and send the worker's 0xBEEF event. Host flips rose from 310 to 476 and the game reached the title. This behavior still needs a proper contract test and a documented rationale (or replacement) before closure.

**Evidence.**
- Host: frame 450 software PPM shows the Gungnir title key art (32 draws, 21 textured); frame 60/ATLUS/logo screens render correctly. `test_boot` frame-60 assertion still green; `ge_vulkan_tests`, `ge_state_machine_tests`, `hle_kernel_tests` green with the new contracts.
- Device: storage-check text and publisher logo render upright at the correct aspect; the user confirms the title path now works. The app reports guest flips at ~20 fps on the title (60 frames per 3 s).
- Device audio is the open problem. Instrumented log at ~15 s: `pulled=670277 underrun=19741 submitted=1273 overruns=0 rejected=0 peak=0 xruns=0`. `peak=0` means every buffer reaching `MixerSink` was silent in that run, so the audible distortion reported earlier is not reproduced by this instrumentation yet. The title exercises `sceAtracDecodeData` heavily (1.18M calls in a 2.5M-dispatch host run), plus `__sceSasCore` and `sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking`; ATRAC streaming/decode and pacing are the prime suspects.

**References used.**
- PPSSPP `Common/GPU/Vulkan/VulkanContext.cpp` (preTransform/rotation), `Core/HLE/sceKernelThread.cpp` (callbacks/scheduling), `Core/HLE/sceUtility.cpp` (savedata status), `Core/Dialog/SavedataParam.h` (savedata mode enum), `GPU/Software/Sampler.cpp` (swizzle/CLUT4).
- Themaister/Granite `vulkan/wsi.cpp` (Android SUBOPTIMAL handling).
- JPCSP `sceUtility.java` (`GetStatus` keeps returning NONE after shutdown).
- jrouwe/JoltPhysics `RendererVK.cpp` (preTransform usage).
- uofw `include/video/lib_mpeg.h` (MPEG error codes), `pspdev/pspsdk` (`psputility_savedata.h`, `ThreadManForUser.S` NID confirmation).

**Next.**
1. Capture the actual PCM the device hears (mixer tap or ATRAC decode dump) and determine whether the distortion is ATRAC decode, silence/gaps, clipping or underrun stutter.
2. Fix ATRAC track decode/streaming and/or mixer pacing; re-check peak/underrun/xrun counters at the title and in the first menu.
3. Verify touch and gamepad menu navigation, overlay hide-on-pad, and title -> menu -> first gameplay transition; capture hashed evidence.
4. Gate or remove temporary diagnostics (savedata stderr trace, msgpipe/vblank traces, histogram limit, boot_runner texture helpers) and add the CheckCallback scheduling test.
5. Run the full suite and clean-checkout gates; update `docs/BRINGUP.md`, `docs/QA.md`, `docs/HLE.md` (MPEG gap, CheckCallback yield) and the T13b report.

## Progress 2026-11-01 (T13b audio and NEW GAME)

**Audio mixer was serialising channels.** `MixerSink` appended every channel
to one FIFO. The title feeds channel 4 (silence) and channel 5 (music) at
44.1 kHz each, so the FIFO gained ~59 k frames/s, filled, and `submit()`
returned false; the HLE stopped the session with `audio sink rejected a
buffer` at ~16 s. The serialised channels were the audible garble. The mixer
is now a timeline mixer: per-channel cursors, 32-bit summation, a 46 ms lead,
a counted resync when a channel falls behind and a counted restart when the
timeline outgrows the ring. `peak` now measures the mixed output. Red-first
evidence: the new two-channel-sum and overflow contracts fail against the HEAD
FIFO and pass with the timeline mixer.

**Descriptor pool exhaustion.** The title froze at ~16 s with
`render_failed: texture descriptor failed (-1000069000)`
(`VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY`). The pool had 64 sets and no
`VK_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_FREE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_BIT`, so freed texture sets
never returned. The pool is now 4096 sets with the free flag.
`ge_vulkan_tests.many_textures` uploads 96 distinct textures; it failed at
texture 63 on the old pool and passes now.

**ATRAC decode starvation.** After those fixes the picture stopped at frame
420 with `SOUND thread(UMD)` (priority 16) spinning at `0x0883AAC0` and
`user_main` (priority 32) merely ready. `sceAtracDecodeData` returned
immediately on success and on `SCE_ATRAC_BUFFER_IS_EMPTY`; the track was
opened with 128 KiB of a 959016-byte data chunk, so after 176 frames the
decode loop returned empty forever. Every decode attempt now waits for the
media engine (`1815 + bytes*158/100` us stereo ATRAC3+, `970 + bytes*44/100`
stereo ATRAC3). After the fix `user_main` runs, all sound threads wait on
audio/delay, and frames advance past the title.

**NEW GAME path.** With the mixer and decode pacing fixed, touch Cross on the
title selects NEW GAME, the game renders the difficulty screen (BASIC /
ADVANCE), and music keeps playing (`peak=23278`, `underruns=0` after startup,
`xruns=0`). The first NEW GAME transition executed
`sceSasCore::__sceSasSetADSRmode`, which used to be an unbound gap; the eight
SAS ADSR/noise/reverb controls are now bound with PSP validation (noise
silent, reverb stored but not mixed, decay always exponential).

**Current blocker.** Confirming a difficulty (Cross) faults inside guest code:
`Guest memory access outside PSP RAM/EDRAM at 0x20` at `0x088FFF64`, a0=0.
The getter at `0x088040A4` returns a null object (global at `0x08A22EF4`,
field +0x5C) and the caller dereferences `this+0x20`. This is the new-game
initialisation path, not the title/menu path.

**Still to do.** Remove the temporary `[session] heartbeat` and `atrac`
device traces, verify the D-pad hit region (centre taps are dead; the down
sector is below centre), record device QA, run the full suite and
`repository_check`, and update `docs/BRINGUP.md` / `docs/HLE.md` (already
updated for the mixer, pool, decode pacing and SAS controls).

**Verification and gates (final T13b device checkpoint).** Touch input is
verified on the M2102K1AC: Cross on the title opens the new-game path, and a
touch on the down sector of the on-screen d-pad moves the difficulty
selection (the centre is a dead zone by design). The pitch/text stays upright
and music plays with `peak=23278 overruns=0 rejected=0 xruns=0`. Final APK
SHA-256 `66d61a495a495d6491699efcfe194165a3ed938d79681d4d150cad63e7e5f419`;
device record `docs/qa/2026-11-01-t13b-title.md`. Host gates: full suite 160
tests OK (11 skipped), `tools/repository_check.py` PASS (386 files),
`git diff --check` clean. Temporary heartbeat/ATRAC tracing is removed; the
only remaining diagnostics are the one-shot session stop reason and the
AAudio stream configuration line.
result: Title screen, music, touch menu and difficulty selection verified on the M2102K1AC (Android 14, Adreno). The title key art and text render upright at the fitted 16:9 aspect; music plays with peak=23278, no rejected buffers and no xruns; touch Cross opens NEW GAME and the on-screen d-pad moves the difficulty selection. Four defects found and fixed red-first: (1) MixerSink serialised channels in one FIFO, filling it at ~59k frames/s and stopping the session ('audio sink rejected a buffer'); it is now a per-channel timeline mixer with 32-bit summation, a 46 ms lead, counted resyncs and counted overflow restarts. **Work:** `tools/intake/`: (1) **disc input = ISO only** (locked decision §1: `game.chd` is converted user-side via [CHDStudio](https://github.com/purelogiccode/CHDStudio) or `chdman extractcd`; intake refuses `.chd` with a named error pointing at `docs/INTAKE.md`; we never parse CHD — the identity gate *verifies, not trusts*, the converter); (2) identity gate: size 262,766,592 + CRC32 `183F3EDC`, **fail closed** on mismatch; (3) ISO9660 extract of `PSP_GAME/` tree (EBOOT.BIN, USRDIR `*.dar`, INSDIR, PARAM.SFO — verify disc ID ULUS-10592); (4) decrypt hook — **no decryption code in-repo**; invoke user-supplied pspdecrypt/PPSSPP "Dump decrypted EBOOT.BIN" out-of-process, accept `BOOT.BIN` plaintext or user-provided decrypted ELF, validate PRX shape (`e_type 0xFFA0`, `vaddr = file_offset − 0xC0`, reloc section `0x70000020`, types 2/5/6); (5) `build/game/manifest.json`: module list, SHA-256s, segments, reloc counts, NID import inventory. All outputs under `build/` (gitignored).
**Test cases:**
- TC-3.1 End-to-end on local `game.iso` produces manifest.json with expected module set. *(Covered by `tests/test_intake.py` — written and observed red before implementation.)*
- TC-3.2 Wrong-CRC input (bit-flipped ISO) aborts with named error `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`; `.chd` input aborts with named error `CHD_NOT_SUPPORTED` pointing at CHDStudio.
- TC-3.3 Truncated/decrypted-partially ELF rejected (magic + program-header checks): `~PSP` magic → `ENCRYPTED_EXECUTABLE` (points at out-of-process decrypt), truncated/garbage → `ELF_INVALID`.
- TC-3.4 Every intermediate artifact lands under `build/`; `repository_check` still green.
**Findings (2026-10-30, from implementation):** ISO9660 + ELF32 + PARAM.SFO parsing is **adopted** from TeamGDB/Yakumo (MIT, `third_party/yakumo/`, pin `b61852a`) — not clean-room, per §1 Code reuse. Intake shape is therefore a C++ reader tool (`tools/intake/intake_tool.cpp`, subcommands `iso-extract`/`elf-inspect`/`sfo-info`, built by root `CMakeLists.txt`) + Python orchestrator (`tools/intake/intake.py`: identity gate + manifest via stdlib `zlib`/`hashlib`/`json` — existing implementations). Known gap: vendored `elf32.cpp` handles reloc section `0x700000A0` only; Gungnir's EBOOT uses `0x70000020` — intake counts both via its own section walk (`ElfSection` list + raw entry scan), vendored code stays unpatched (recorded in `third_party/yakumo/PROVENANCE.md`). Manifest records the actual section type found, for T5.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/INTAKE.md` (user-facing: how to supply their own disc, external decrypt tools, what the gates check).
**Refs:** gungnir-ptbr (ISO offsets, `~PSP` layout — facts only), wtf-psp-recomp (`extract.ps1` report style), Yakumo (`prepare_game.sh` SHA-pin pattern), codepdbh (`--verify-only` identity gate).
**Gotchas:** §7B (format traps), §7A.1–A.3.

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1). Clean-room reimplementations of existing formats/codecs/protocols are NOT sanctioned (plan §0.6 / AGENTS.md #0) — adopt audited open-source code with provenance or stop and ask.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.
result: T3 complete. Deliverables: tools/intake/intake_tool.cpp (C++ reader: iso-extract / elf-inspect / sfo-info over vendored yakumo subset) + tools/intake/intake.py (orchestrator: identity gate size 262766592 + CRC32 183F3EDC streaming, ISO extract, PARAM.SFO disc-id gate ULUS-10592, decrypt boundary, manifest.json). Red-first: test_intake.py observed red before implementation (pre-commit red evidence in prior session); suite green: TC-3.1 end-to-end on real game.iso (manifest module set incl. EBOOT.BIN; sysdir execs covered; sha256 cross-checks), TC-3.2 wrong-CRC/sizes abort IDENTITY_MISMATCH + .chd aborted CHD_NOT_SUPPORTED with CHDStudio guidance, TC-3.3 encrypted/truncated/garbage rejected by name (ENCRYPTED_EXECUTABLE / ELF_INVALID), TC-3.4 artifacts confined to build/ + repository_check green. Facts recorded from the real disc: BOOT.BIN not plaintext ELF (manifest status UNRECOGNIZED_SHAPE = counted gap), decrypted EBOOT uses reloc type 0x700000A0 (49,396 entries, both A0/20 accepted; plan's predicted 0x70000020 did not occur), module regimes differ (updater runtime-absolute fields, main '9th' module-relative), disc ships SYSDIR/UPDATE/{EBOOT.BIN,PARAM.SFO,DATA.BIN}. Vendored guest_memory.cpp byte-identically (pinned b61852a) to satisfy elf32.cpp link; embedder seam (runtime_thread_uid/name, runtime_dispatch_pc) defined inert per PROVENANCE.md. Decrypt boundary per plan §0.3: pspdecrypt on PATH/~/.local/bin or --decrypt-tool '{in} {out}' template or env GUNGNIR_DECRYPT_TOOL; plaintext BOOT.BIN sibling accepted only when it parses as ELF; no decryption in-repo. Stripped-ELF module-info located via content-anchored candidates validated functionally by the vendored import walker (main module: 215 NIDs, updater: 158). Docs checkpoint: docs/INTAKE.md. Commits: 1d5644f.

name: T12a — Audio: SAS/ATRAC/MP3 synthesis and device output
description:
Part of 'Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan' (epic). Plan section T12a (.dex/plan.md §5); the parent T12 is split into audio (T12a) and savedata/DAR (T12b).

# T12a — Audio: SAS/ATRAC/MP3 synthesis and device output

**Depends on:** T6 (T6h vendored ATRAC decoder, T6g/T6m SAS core/envelopes, T6f sceAudio channels already landed)
**Work:** `runtime/audio/`: finish sceSasCore 32-voice VAG/ADPCM synthesis (pitch/ADSR — the T6g/T6m slice exists; close the remaining voice/effect calls the title executes), complete the sceAtrac3plus track calls over the vendored FFmpeg n4.4 decoder (T6l left SetData/DecodeData/GetRemainFrame/GetStreamDataInfo/AddStreamData/SetLoopNum as a counted gap; add the full track API and never fake PCM), sceMp3 (parse + decode via an adopted decoder, or a named counted gap if the title never calls it), and mix everything to one 44.1 kHz stream feeding an AAudio low-latency callback on Android / SDL audio on desktop. Ring buffer, fade-in/out and error-callback restart; underrun accounting, no hidden stalls.
**Test cases:**
- TC-12.1 SAS voice unit tests (ADPCM decode, pitch, ADSR envelope shapes).
- TC-12.2 Audio smoke: tone + VAG playback via AAudio on device, SDL on desktop; no underruns in a 60 s soak at 59.94 pacing.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/AUDIO.md` (voice model, codec coverage, sink contract, underrun policy, counted gaps).
**Refs:** sp00nznet (sascore), sal063 (audio.c), snuri00 (at3_standalone + SAS), codepdbh (AAudio path), psprecore (`runtime/src/audio/sas.cpp` SPU-rate envelopes, `hle_atrac.cpp`/`hle_mpeg.cpp` — MIT; its cccook decodes offline, not at runtime), FFmpeg n4.4 (vendored decoder; LGPL notices/relink).
**Gotchas:** §7E.4 (AAudio underruns), §7F.5 (ATRAC edge-case decode quirk).

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): test cases observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Device validation: see `android/AGENTS.md` — emulator is for initial bring-up; physical arm64 phone QA is required at sprint end and recorded in `docs/qa/`. Reproducible emulator: `scripts/android/emulator.sh`.
result:
T12a complete (audio code through 7f755ea; AAudio QA 2ed55dd/380b58e; suite dedupe c0b9ee9).

- SAS: the MIT Yakumo core provides 32 VAG/ADPCM voices with pitch, ADSR, looping and no reverb; sceAudio channels and the source-merge path are covered by host tests.
- Output: MixerSink turns sceAudio buffers into one 44.1 kHz stereo ring with per-channel volume, mono duplication, underrun accounting and loud overflow rejection. SDL3 (`runtime/platform/sdl_audio.*`) and AAudio (`runtime/platform/android/aaudio_out.*`) backends feed it. A 60 s phone soak pulled 2,647,610 frames with underrun=0 and AAudio xruns=0; a 20 s 440 Hz run was confirmed audible at full media volume.
- ATRAC: `runtime/audio/atrac_file.*` parses RIFF/WAVE ATRAC3 (0x270) and ATRAC3+ (0xFFFE), including fact totals/delay, smpl loops and codec extra data, and drives the vendored FFmpeg n4.4 decoder. sceAtrac3plus implements GetAtracID, SetData/SetDataAndGetID, SetHalfwayBuffer(AndGetID), Release, GetSoundSample, GetChannel, GetMaxSample, GetRemainFrame, GetNextSample, GetNextDecodePosition, GetBitrate, GetLoopStatus, SetLoopNum, ResetPlayPosition, DecodeData, GetStreamDataInfo, AddStreamData, GetBufferInfoForReseting, GetSecondBufferInfo/SetSecondBuffer (not needed because all streamed bytes are retained), StartEntry/EndEntry and GetInternalErrorInfo. DecodeData cuts guest PCM at frame/loop/end boundaries and returns 0x80630024 after the last frame; malformed input is a named error, never fake PCM.
- Test cases: TC-12.1 SAS ADPCM/pitch/ADSR contracts; TC-12.2 SDL/AAudio tone smoke plus the 60 s no-underrun device soak. Host gates `tests.test_audio`, `tests.test_audio_mixer`, `tests.test_sdl_audio`, `tests.test_hle`.
- Named gaps: game-loop 59.94 Hz pacing and real game audio are T13; `sceMp3` is absent from GUNGNIR's import inventory, so no MP3 implementation was warranted; KIRK/secure audio is out of scope.

References: Yakumo MIT SAS core (pinned b61852a), Nakagawa/FFmpeg n4.4 ATRAC decoder (LGPL-2.1-or-later), psprecore and PPSSPP ATRAC buffer semantics (behavioral only; no code copied), 3rd Birthday ATRAC buffer model (GPL/PPSSPP-derived, behavioral only).

# T13c — BUILDING.md and ANDROID.md

**Depends on:** T13a, T13b.

**Goal.** A new contributor with their own legally obtained disc can follow one document from an empty machine to the title screen.

**Work.**
- Write `docs/BUILDING.md`: prerequisites and pinned toolchain, dependency materialization/verification, ISO-only intake, user-side decryption (external tool, never in-repo), analysis, AOT codegen, Linux build/boot, Android build with `-Pgungnir.gameCorpus`, install/run/screenshot, offline mode, clean rebuild, and every named failure code. Include exact commands and expected output lines; no absolute machine paths, no game hashes or screenshots.
- Finalize `docs/ANDROID.md`: the T13 runtime chain, corpus/synthetic modes, memstick root, bounded-run logs and intent extras, emulator vs physical device, QA links, and current named gaps.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- The doc test fails before the files exist and before each newly documented flag exists.
- A command in the doc is executed in dry-run/`--help` form where possible; a stale flag fails the test.
- `repository_check` PASS after the docs land.

**Acceptance.** An independent reader can follow the document; every command is copy-pasteable with placeholders clearly marked; the doc contract test is green.

**Guardrails.** No game text, screenshots, hashes, keys or URLs that advertise a dump. No claim without evidence in the tree. Keep audience-facing docs free of internal task jargon.

**Docs.** `docs/BUILDING.md`, `docs/ANDROID.md`, README links.

**Reference projects (document shape).**
- `Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp` (GPL-3.0) — from-scratch BUILDING/README command flow and Android property documentation.
- `TeamGDB/Yakumo` (MIT) — `prepare_game.sh` pin/verify workflow and installer documentation.
- `Jstar269/hst-decomp` (GPL-3.0) — toolchain-lock re-verification wording so the doc matches the gate.
- `AdamFull/ff7ccrecomp` (MIT) — user-facing build/deploy documentation and known-gap presentation.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Read the matching source with `gh repo read-file` / `gh repo read-dir`, never raw.githubusercontent.com. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).

all nine checks failed on `docs/BUILDING.md is missing`. The contract now
checks that the guide exists, that every script it names exists, that every

**Guardrails.** No key material. No rumble that fires on menu focus or overlay edits. Do not claim device feedback without a physical-device observation.

name: T8d — Replacement loader for user PNGs at any resolution
description:
Depends on: T8a, T8c.

Load user PNG replacements from the replacement folder using the same
content key as dump mode. A replacement at any resolution (2x/4x included)
takes precedence over the guest texture; sampling follows GE state for
filter/clamp and must not assume the replacement matches native dimensions.
A PNG with no matching key is reported by name (log line, counted) rather
than silently ignored; a corrupt PNG fails closed with a named error. Dump
mode must never clobber an existing replacement.

Tests (red first):
- TC-8.2 reload half: dump -> replace -> reload in the Linux runtime with a
  synthetic scene; the replacement pixels reach the rendered frame.
- 2x and 4x replacements win over the native texture and scale correctly.
- Key mismatch is reported and leaves the native texture active.
- Corrupt PNG fails closed; removing the precedence rule fails the test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "texture_replacement" --extension cpp`;
`gh search code "textures.ini" --extension cpp`; `gh search issues
"texture replacement scaling"`; `gh search code "png_load" --extension cpp`.

Refs: psprecore texture_replacement.cpp (MIT, behavioral reference),
ff7ccrecomp `tools/psptex` HD layering behavior, T7 Vulkan texture upload
path. Gotchas: §7A.2, §7D.2 (bufw/CLUT correctness).
result:
Added runtime/tex/{replace.hpp,replace.cpp} and the gungnir_tex_replace target. TextureReplacements loads replace/<KEY>.png (also lowercase/.PNG) for the T8c content key, accepts any resolution, and normalises user PNGs to RGBA8 through the shared libpng reader. ReplacementImage::state_for copies the live clamp/filter state and overrides format to RGBA8, swizzle off, and width/height/buffer width to the replacement, so the GE sampling path handles 2x/4x images without a separate scaler. Successful loads are cached until clear()/set_root(); native textures remain the fallback.

find() fails closed with named errors: invalid_root, invalid_key, not_found, file_access_failed, invalid_replacement, and PNG errors (png_read_failed/png_unsupported_layout/file_not_found). scan(known_keys) reports present PNGs, loaded known keys, unmatched PNG filenames (sorted) and per-file errors (sorted), so unknown/corrupt files are counted rather than dropped. Dump mode never writes under replace/.

Tests in tests/tex/replace_tests.cpp: 2x and 4x replacements rendered through the software rasterizer with the expected block pattern, native fallback, state derivation and clamp/filter copying, unmatched/corrupt scan reporting, cache/clear reload, dump/replacement isolation, missing replace directory and invalid keys/roots. Mutation: dropping the replacement width/height fails 'replacement state uses the image dimensions'. Local check: a 256x56 container texture dumped and loaded as a 512x112 replacement (scan loaded=1, no errors). Full suite 78/78 green; repository_check PASS (227 files).

References used: psprecore runtime/src/gpu/texture_replacement.cpp (MIT) for 16-hex keyed folder scanning, any-resolution PNG loading and cache/worker shape (behavior only; no code copied), PPSSPP PR #8715, the texture-replacement wiki and GPU/Common/TextureReplacer.cpp for pack semantics (hashranges/filtering/mipmaps remain unimplemented; no code adopted), LiinkPK/Texture-Replacement-Tool-for-PPSSPP for pack workflow (binary-only), the T8c content key, and libpng for decoding. docs/TEXTURE_REPLACEMENT.md now documents the replace/ layout, key rules, API, errors, cache/reload and dump isolation.

name: T12b — Savedata and DAR asset support
description:
Part of 'Gungnir Recomp — Master Plan' (epic). Plan section T12b (.dex/plan.md §5); the parent T12 is split into audio (T12a) and savedata/DAR (T12b).

# T12b — Savedata and DAR asset support

**Depends on:** T6 (T6k savedata SIZES/dialog state machine already landed)
**Work:** (1) `runtime/savedata/`: virtual memstick `PSP/SAVEDATA/<title>/` with PARAM.SFO v1.1 (PSF) read/write and a PPSSPP-compatible layout (saves interchangeable with emulator/hardware); complete the savedata modes the title executes beyond the T6k SIZES slice; KIRK save encryption **deferred**, documented honestly (hash-left-zero stance — never ship key material). (2) `tools/dar.py` for the asset pipeline (both DAR sides: read/list/extract + in-place rewrite rules; `stored_size==0` = uncompressed). Size-preserving in-place rewrite with zero-filled tail and named errors; every writer proves a byte-identical round-trip before it may write a new payload. A host compatibility harness mounts the user's PPSSPP memstick exports read-only and copies them into a scratch root so tests never mutate the originals.
**Test cases:**
- TC-12.3 Save→load round-trip byte-stable; PARAM.SFO opens in PPSSPP.
- TC-12.4 `dar.py` lists/extracts the user's `ini.dar`; a repack round-trips byte-identically; the `stored_size==0` entries survive.
- TC-12.5 PPSSPP memstick interchange: copy the user's exported saves (`savestates/ULUS10592GUN9THSYS` and `savestates/ULUS10592GUN9THSTORY00`) into a scratch `ms0:/PSP/SAVEDATA/` root, list both through the virtual memstick, parse each PARAM.SFO, and parse→serialize each file byte-identically; then save→load→save leaves every save file byte-identical. The export is never mutated in place. A save written by our runtime into PPSSPP's memstick is listed and loadable by PPSSPP (oracle).
- TC-12.6 PPSSPP oracle: use a PPSSPP 1.20.4 clean boot (the supplied `.ppst` resumes before a battle, where no save menu exists) to list and load the exported SYSTEM/STORY saves (`ULUS10592GUN9THSYS`, `ULUS10592GUN9THSTORY00`, 61,888-byte STORY), then repeat with the tree rewritten by `SaveStore`; every rewritten file is SHA-256-identical to the export. The `.ppst` container is PPSSPP-specific and is never parsed in-repo (a clean-room reimplementation needs explicit sign-off). Evidence: `docs/qa/2026-10-31-t12b-savedata.md`.
**Local fixtures:** the exported savestate and both memstick saves live under gitignored `savestates/`; they are the user's own data, never committed, copied into a temp memstick for tests, and any case that needs them skips with the named reason `savedata_fixture_missing` when absent.
**Docs checkpoint:** `docs/SAVEDATA.md`, `docs/formats/DAR.md` (extended from T3/T8).
**Refs:** sal063 (savedata.c/PARAM.SFO), gungnir-ptbr (DAR traps), psprecore (`hle_savedata.cpp` SceUtilitySavedataParam offsets/modes — MIT; its save layout omits the `PSP/` prefix), PPSSPP (PARAM.SFO/save-layout oracle, behavioral only — no code).
**Gotchas:** §7B.1 (DAR `stored_size==0`), §7B.2 (in-place rewrite), §7B.3 (script `.bin` sizes), §7B.4 (both-endian ISO sizes).

Red-first rule applies (plan §8.1): test cases observed red before implementation; bug fixes start with a reproducing red test.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Device validation: see `android/AGENTS.md` — emulator is for initial bring-up; physical arm64 phone QA is required at sprint end and recorded in `docs/qa/`. Reproducible emulator: `scripts/android/emulator.sh`.
result:
T12b complete (savedata 5d78197, DAR c2123f1, PPSSPP oracle 414d9a1).

- `runtime/savedata/save_store.*`: PSP/SAVEDATA layout with validated names, symlink rejection, sorted listings, atomic per-file writes and the vendored MIT PARAM.SFO reader/writer. The SFO carries TITLE, SAVEDATA_TITLE, SAVEDATA_DETAIL, PARENTAL_LEVEL, CATEGORY=MS, SAVEDATA_DIRECTORY, the 99-entry file list and zeroed SAVEDATA_PARAMS; parse->serialize is byte-identical for exported PSP saves.
- sceUtilitySavedata implements SIZES plus LOAD (SFO fields, bind=1021, data/icons) and SAVE (data, icons/pic/snd, fresh SFO) with named PSP error codes. LIST/DELETE/picker modes remain documented gaps.
- `tools/dar.py` lists, extracts and size-preservingly repacks DAR archives: nested names, zlib and stored payloads, stored_size==0, zero-filled tails, unchanged-entry byte identity and named failures (traversal, oversized blob, stored-size change). The user's INI.DAR round-trips with an unchanged hash.
- Test cases: TC-12.3 save/load byte-stable and SFO round-trip; TC-12.4 DAR list/extract/repack with byte-identical untouched and real-archive runs; TC-12.5 exported PPSSPP saves mount/list/parse/rewrite byte-identically; TC-12.6 a PPSSPP 1.20.4 clean boot lists and loads ULUS10592GUN9THSYS and ULUS10592GUN9THSTORY00 (61,888-byte STORY) and loads the tree rewritten by SaveStore; every rewritten file is SHA-256-identical to the export. A savestate boot resumes before a battle and is not a load oracle.
- Docs: docs/SAVEDATA.md, docs/formats/DAR.md, docs/qa/2026-10-31-t12b-savedata.md.
- Named gaps: KIRK/secure save encryption and real-PSP secure saves are deferred; LIST/DELETE/picker modes are not implemented; the Android memory-stick root is wired with the HLE in T13.

description:

# T13e — Hygiene gates

**Depends on:** T13d.

**Goal.** A deliberate game-artifact commit is blocked locally and in CI, and the tree proves license/notice/SPDX coverage without leaking secrets.

**Work.**

- Add a secret scan (gitleaks or equivalent, pinned action/binary by SHA) with an explicit, reviewed allowlist. Cover PSP key material patterns, keystores, tokens and private keys. A finding fails the job; do not suppress wholesale.
- Wire license/notice coverage (`tools/package_notices.py check-coverage` and `check-licenses`) and `repository_check` into the same required job.
- Introduce SPDX/REUSE lint: add `REUSE.toml` mapping first-party files to GPL-3.0-or-later and preserving third-party licenses/notices; pin `reuse` in CI; ensure vendored files keep their own identifiers. No relicensing.
- Extend tests: `tests/test_repository_check.py` dummy-artifact cases, a new `tests/test_reuse.py` (coverage + `reuse lint`), and a workflow assertion that every hygiene gate is present and fail-closed.
- Update `docs/LEGAL.md`/`docs/PROVENANCE.md` with the gate list and how to add a dependency without breaking coverage.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- Dummy `.iso`, `.elf` and `~PSP` staged in a scratch repo are rejected with named errors, locally and in the CI scenario.
- A CC BY-NC-SA component is rejected (existing TC-2.3) and an unlisted `third_party/` file is rejected (TC-2.2) in CI.
- A planted fake secret in a scratch file is caught; a reviewed allowlist entry passes without hiding other findings.
- `reuse lint` is clean; removing a license mapping fails the test.
- Mutation check: disable one gate in a scratch copy and confirm the hygiene test dies for that reason.

**Acceptance / evidence.** Local gate and CI job both block dummy artifacts; secret/license/notice/SPDX gates are required; no real secret or key material is present; docs describe the gates.

**Guardrails.** Never add key material, even as a test value — use clearly fake placeholders. Do not commit third-party binaries. Do not add a gate that only checks for a string while ignoring the actual index.

**Docs.** `docs/LEGAL.md`, `docs/PROVENANCE.md`, `docs/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md`, `REUSE.toml`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`.

**Reference projects (hygiene patterns).**
- `Jstar269/hst-decomp` (GPL-3.0) — `REUSE.toml` licensing layout and manifest discipline.
- `zxyandreay/azazel6` (MIT) — `repository_check.py` magic-byte/blob-size/ignore-probe/secret audit.
- `Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp` (GPL-3.0) — notices generated from one JSON source of truth and the CI hygiene matrix.

**Research first (required).** Before writing code, run `gh search code "<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"` for semantics and regressions. PPSSPP, the 3rd Birthday recomp and Metal Gear Acid 2 are behavioral oracles only — never vendored or linked — and a clean-room reimplementation of an existing format, codec or protocol is not sanctioned without explicit user sign-off (AGENTS.md #0).
Specific first searches: `gh search code "REUSE.toml" --filename "REUSE.toml"`, `gh repo read-file "REUSE.toml" --repo Jstar269/hst-decomp`, `gh search code "gitleaks" --filename "*.yml"`, `gh search issues "REUSE lint vendored"` and `"gitleaks allowlist false positive"`. name: T13d — CI build matrix: Linux + Android cross-compile with fail-closed private inputs
description:
Part of T13 (plan §5). Owns TC-13.2 and the `exit 77` contract.

# T13d — CI build matrix and fail-closed private inputs

**Depends on:** T13a.

**Goal.** A clean clone with zero game artifacts builds and tests on GitHub Actions, and a missing private input can never look like a pass.

**Work.**
- Add GitHub Actions workflows (Linux runtime + Android cross-compile) on push/PR: pinned JDK/SDK/NDK/CMake, dependency materialization with digest verification, Linux build + full synthetic suite, Android APK build with the synthetic corpus, `repository_check`.
- Pin every action to a full commit SHA with a version comment; minimum permissions; concurrency cancellation; no secrets; no `pull_request_target` with secret access. Upload only logs/reports, never game frames or generated code.
- Implement the fail-closed private-input contract: CMake `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77` for private-input tests; Python tests honor `GUNGNIR_REQUIRE_PRIVATE_INPUT=1` and turn a skipped private case into a hard failure (or exit 77 where the harness maps it); CI sets strict mode in jobs without game data. Document the convention in `docs/TESTING.md`.
- Prove a clean clone: a job lists tracked files and asserts no `.iso/.chd/.elf/.prx/.bin/.dar/.tpl` or generated corpus; `repository_check` runs on the same tree. No submodules or LFS game blobs.
- Add `tests/test_ci_workflows.py` (red first): workflows exist, actions are SHA-pinned, strict mode is set, Android job uses the synthetic corpus, no secret-bearing triggers, no game paths. Add `tests/test_private_inputs.py` for strict-mode skip conversion.

**Test cases (red-first).**
- Workflow contract test fails before the workflow files exist and when an action is tag-pinned.
- Strict-mode test fails a deliberately skipping private test; non-strict local run still skips cleanly.
- Clean-clone artifact scan fails on a deliberately added dummy `.iso` under a scan fixture.
- TC-13.2: capture the green run on a clean clone and record the run URL/log pointer and the file-count/artifact evidence.

**Acceptance / evidence.** CI is green on a clean clone with zero game artifacts; `repository_check` proves the tracked tree; Android APK built with synthetic fixtures only; private-input tests are fail-closed in CI.

**Guardrails.** Never place game data, keys, driver zips or generated code on runners. Do not require a physical device for CI. Do not weaken a gate to make CI green; fix the cause.

**Docs.** `docs/TESTING.md` (skip contract), `docs/ANDROID.md` (CI build mode), `.github/workflows/*`.

**Reference projects (CI policy).**
- `Jstar269/nakagawa-recomp` (GPL-3.0) — `exit 77` fail-closed skips and synthetic-fixture-only CI.
- `TeamGDB/Yakumo` (MIT) — multi-platform CI/release automation and pinned-dependency jobs.
- `Jstar269/hst-decomp` (GPL-3.0) — toolchain-lock re-verification in CI.
- `zxyandreay/azazel6` (MIT) — `repository_check` merge gate, bounded-run and evidence policy.

silently mis-decoded.

Write docs/formats/TPL.md from the user's local files at layout level only:
offsets, field meanings, swizzle rule, CLUT layout. No TPL bytes, no game
textures, no dump hashes in the repository.

Tests (red first, synthetic fixtures of our authorship):
- TC-8.1 decode half: synthetic containers decode to hand-computed pixels.
- TC-8.4 edge cases: odd widths, multi-texture n_tex > 1, bpp=4 alpha ramp,
  bpp=5 CLUT decode.
- Malformed header/offset/data_off cases fail with named errors.

Reference discovery (all tasks): before implementing, use `gh search code
"<api-or-symbol>"` (add `--extension cpp` for C/C++ HLE work) to find concrete
implementations and their projects, then `gh search issues "<api-or-symbol>"`
for semantics and regressions. Record the references used.

Specific searches: `gh search code "tpl" --extension cpp`; `gh search code
"texture swizzle" --extension cpp`; `gh search code "palette 16" --extension
cpp`; `gh search issues "PSP texture swizzle"`; `gh search code
"texture_collection" --extension cpp`.

Refs: psprecore `runtime/src/gpu/texture_collection.cpp` and `texture.cpp`
(MIT, behavioral reference), gungnir-ptbr TPL/DAR facts, PPSSPP texture
decode behavior (diff oracle only, never linked). Gotchas: §7B.2-B.4, §7F.3,
§7F.4 (bpp=5 CLUT layout).
result:
Added runtime/tex/{tpl.hpp,tpl.cpp} and the gungnir_tex target. Decodes the n_texture/table header, 0x14-byte texture descriptors (H/W/BW/pixel-format/data offset plus preserved opaque bytes), 8-byte palette descriptors and swizzled CLUT4/CLUT8 data through the shared T7d GE texture decoder. Palette CLUT masks derive from entry count; RGB565/RGBA5551/RGBA4444/RGBA8888 palettes supported. 0xFFFF auxiliary entries are counted in Tpl::resources with bounded sizes and never silently dropped. Named failures cover truncated tables, bad offsets, unsupported formats (DXT/0x0108), invalid dimensions, partial swizzle geometry, invalid palettes and missing CLUT palettes. Tpl::bytes and raw descriptor bytes are preserved for the T8b writer.

Tests: tests/tex/tpl_tests.cpp (built by tests/test_tpl.py) covers synthetic CLUT4 alpha ramps at odd width, RGB565 and RGBA8888 palettes, CLUT8, multi-texture containers, resource counting and malformed inputs. Mutation check: fixing the CLUT mask at 16 entries fails 'CLUT mask selects all 256 entries'. Full suite 76/76 green; repository_check PASS (216 files). Local ASan/UBSan scan of the user's extracted TPLs decoded 1,886 textures / 58,952,576 pixels from 1,304 of 1,305 unique containers; only debugFont.tpl (pixel format 0x0108) fails closed and is recorded as a named gap in docs/formats/TPL.md.

References used: kreycai/gungnir-ptbr tools/fonte_gungnir.py and docs/graficos_com_texto.md (header fields, 4bpp swizzle, alpha-ramp palette), local header inspection of INI.DAR/DATA.DAR (table/palette layout, multi-texture and 0xFFFF resource sentinel; no bytes copied), marco-calautti/Rainbow TPLTexture.Serializer.cs (structurally comparable multi-image TPL only; it is the Nintendo format, not the Gungnir PSP variant), LiinkPK/Texture-Replacement-Tool-for-PPSSPP (binary-only replacement UX for T8c/T8d, no source adopted), PPSSPP PR #8715/wiki (textures.ini semantics for T8c/T8d), PPSSPP image-formats doc (GE TPF numbering).
